He also took away the leading men of the land, 14so that the kingdom would stay lowly and not rise up again, but would keep his covenant and so survive. 15But he rebelled against him by sending envoys to Egypt to get horses and a large army. Will he succeed? Will a man who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and still escape? 16As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, it is in Babylon that he will die, in the land of the king who put him on the throne, the king whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke. 17Pharaoh with his mighty army and great horde will not help him in battle, when ramps are heaped up and siege walls are built to destroy many lives. 18He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. Though he had given his hand on it, he did all these things. He will not escape.

Punishment for the broken oath

19Therefore the Lord GOD says this: As surely as I live, I will make him bear the penalty of my oath, which he despised, and of my covenant, which he broke. 20I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon and judge him there for the unfaithfulness he committed against me. 21All the fugitives from his troops will fall by the sword, and those who are left will be scattered in every direction. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.

The tender shoot on the high mountain

22The Lord GOD says this: I myself will take a sprig from the top of the tall cedar and plant it. I will pluck a tender shoot from its topmost twigs, and I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain. 23On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it, and it will put out branches and bear fruit, and it will become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will live under it; they will find shelter in the shade of its branches. 24All the trees of the field will know that I, the LORD, bring down the tall tree and raise up the low tree, dry up the green tree and make the dry tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
fields.summary: A parable of two eagles and a vine pictures the king of Judah’s rebellion against Babylon. God will plant a tender shoot on a high mountain.

fields.title: Ezekiel 18
fields.body_html:
The proverb of the sour grapes

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2What do you mean by repeating this proverb about the land of Israel: “The parents eat sour grapes, but it is the children whose teeth are set on edge”? 3As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, this proverb will no longer be quoted in Israel. 4Every life belongs to me, the life of the parent as well as the life of the child; both belong to me. The person who sins is the one who will die.

A righteous man, his son and his grandson

5Suppose there is a man who is righteous and does what is just and right, 6who does not eat at the mountain shrines or look to the idols of the house of Israel, who does not defile his neighbor’s wife or have relations with a woman during her period, 7who does not oppress anyone but returns what a debtor gave him as a pledge, who does not rob but gives his food to the hungry and clothes the naked, 8who does not lend at interest or take profit, who keeps his hand from wrongdoing and judges fairly between one person and another, 9and who follows my statutes and keeps my rulings faithfully. That man is righteous; he will surely live, declares the Lord GOD. 10But suppose he has a son who is violent, who sheds blood and does any of these things, 11though the father himself did none of them. This son eats at the mountain shrines, defiles his neighbor’s wife, 12oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not return what was pledged, looks to the idols, does detestable things, 13and lends at interest and takes profit. Will such a man live? He will not live! He has done all these detestable things; he will surely be put to death. His blood will be on his own head. 14But suppose this man in turn has a son, and the son sees all the sins his father has committed, and though he sees them, he does not do the same, 15who does not eat at the mountain shrines or look to the idols of the house of Israel, who does not defile his neighbor’s wife, 16who does not oppress anyone or demand a pledge, who does not rob but gives his food to the hungry and clothes the naked, 17who keeps his hand from harming the poor and takes no interest or profit, who obeys my rulings and follows my statutes. He will not die for his father’s guilt; he will surely live. 18But as for his father, he will die for his own guilt, because he extorted from others, robbed his brother and did what was not good among his people. 19Yet you ask, “Why should the son not share the guilt of his father?” The son has done what is just and right and has been careful to keep all my statutes, so he will surely live. 20The person who sins is the one who will die. A child will not share the guilt of a parent, and a parent will not share the guilt of a child. The righteousness of the righteous will be their own, and the wickedness of the wicked will be their own.

When the wicked turn from their sins

21But if wicked people turn away from all the sins they have committed, keep all my statutes and do what is just and right, they will surely live; they will not die. 22None of the rebellious acts they have committed will be remembered against them. Because of the righteousness they have practiced, they will live. 23Is it any pleasure to me when the wicked die? declares the Lord GOD. Would I not rather that they turn from their ways and live?

When the righteous turn away

24But if righteous people turn away from their righteousness and do wrong, committing all the same detestable things that the wicked do, will they live? None of the righteous things they have done will be remembered. Because of the unfaithfulness they are guilty of and the sins they have committed, they will die. 25Yet you say, “The Lord’s way is not fair.” Listen, house of Israel: Is it my way that is not fair? Is it not your ways that are unfair? 26If righteous people turn away from their righteousness and do wrong, they will die for it; because of the wrong they have done, they will die.

Turn and live

27And if wicked people turn away from the wickedness they have committed and do what is just and right, they will save their lives. 28Because they thought it over and turned away from all the rebellious acts they had committed, they will surely live; they will not die. 29Yet the house of Israel says, “The Lord’s way is not fair.” Are my ways unfair, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unfair? 30Therefore, house of Israel, I will judge each of you according to your ways, declares the Lord GOD. Repent and turn away from all your rebellious acts, so that your guilt will not bring you down. 31Throw away all the rebellious acts you have committed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why would you die, house of Israel? 32The death of anyone gives me no pleasure, declares the Lord GOD. So turn back and live!
fields.summary: Each person is responsible for their own sin; the son will not die for the father’s sin. God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked and calls them to turn and live.

fields.title: Ezekiel 19
fields.body_html:
A lament for the princes of Israel

1And you, raise a lament over the princes of Israel,
2and say: What a lioness your mother was!
She lay down among lions;
among young lions she reared her cubs.
3She raised one of her cubs, and he became a young lion.
He learned to tear prey, and he devoured people.
4The nations heard about him, and he was caught in their pit.
They led him with hooks to the land of Egypt.
5When she saw that she had waited in vain and her hope was gone,
she took another of her cubs and made him into a young lion.
6He prowled among the lions and became a young lion.
He learned to tear prey, and he devoured people.
7He preyed on their widows
and laid waste their cities.
The land and everything in it was appalled at the sound of his roaring.
8Then nations from the provinces on every side set themselves against him.
They spread their net over him, and he was caught in their pit.
9With hooks they put him in a cage
and brought him to the king of Babylon.
They put him in a stronghold,
so that his roar would no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel.

The vine uprooted

10Your mother was like a vine in your blood, planted beside water.
It bore fruit and was full of branches
because there was plenty of water.
11Its branches were strong, fit to be rulers’ scepters.
It towered high above the thick branches;
it stood out for its height
and its many branches.
12But it was uprooted in wrath and thrown to the ground.
The east wind dried up its fruit;
its strong branch was broken off and withered, and fire consumed it.
13Now it is planted in the desert,
in a dry and thirsty land.
14Fire has gone out from one of its branches and consumed its shoots and fruit.
No strong branch is left on it, no scepter for ruling.
This is a lament, and it has become a lament.
fields.summary: Ezekiel laments for Israel’s princes, pictured as lion cubs captured and a vine uprooted.

fields.title: Ezekiel 20
fields.body_html:
Elders come to consult the LORD

1In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, a group of Israel’s elders came to consult the LORD, and they sat down in front of me.

2The word of the LORD came to me: 3Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel. Say to them, The Lord GOD says this: Have you come to consult me? As surely as I live, I will not let you consult me, declares the Lord GOD. 4Will you judge them? Will you judge them, son of man? Then make them see the detestable practices of their ancestors. 5Say to them, The Lord GOD says this: On the day I chose Israel, I raised my hand in an oath to the offspring of Jacob’s house and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt. I raised my hand in an oath to them and said, “I am the LORD your God.” 6On that day I swore to them that I would bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land I had scouted out for them, flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands. 7I said to them, “Every one of you must throw away the vile idols you look to, and do not make yourselves unclean with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.” 8But they rebelled against me and refused to listen to me. None of them threw away the vile idols they looked to, and they did not abandon the idols of Egypt. So I said that I would pour out my wrath on them and use up my anger against them there in the land of Egypt. 9But I acted for the sake of my name, to keep it from being dishonored in the eyes of the nations they lived among, the nations in whose sight I had made myself known to Israel by bringing them out of the land of Egypt. 10So I led them out of the land of Egypt and took them into the wilderness. 11I gave them my statutes and taught them my rulings. The one who does them will live by them. 12I also gave them my Sabbaths as a sign between me and them, so that they would know that I am the LORD, the one who sets them apart as holy. 13But in the wilderness the house of Israel rebelled against me. They did not follow my statutes; they rejected my rulings, though the one who does them will live by them, and they utterly dishonored my Sabbaths. So I said that I would pour out my wrath on them in the wilderness and destroy them completely. 14But I acted for the sake of my name, to keep it from being dishonored in the eyes of the nations who had watched me bring them out. 15Also, in the wilderness, I swore an oath to them that I would not lead them into the land I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands, 16because they rejected my rulings, did not follow my statutes and dishonored my Sabbaths. Their hearts were set on their idols. 17Yet I had pity on them and did not destroy them; I did not wipe them out in the wilderness. 18In the wilderness I said to their children, “Do not follow the statutes of your ancestors or keep their rulings, and do not make yourselves unclean with their idols. 19I am the LORD your God. Follow my statutes, and be careful to keep my rulings. 20Keep my Sabbaths holy, and they will be a sign between me and you, so that you will know that I am the LORD your God.” 21But the children rebelled against me too. They did not follow my statutes and were not careful to keep my rulings, though the one who does them will live by them. They dishonored my Sabbaths. So I said that I would pour out my wrath on them and use up my anger against them in the wilderness. 22But I held back my hand and acted for the sake of my name, to keep it from being dishonored in the eyes of the nations who had watched me bring them out. 23In the wilderness I also swore to them that I would scatter them among the nations and spread them through the countries, 24because they had not kept my rulings, had rejected my statutes and dishonored my Sabbaths, and their eyes were set on the idols of their ancestors. 25I also gave them statutes that were not good and rulings by which they could not live. 26I made them unclean through their own gifts, when they gave up every firstborn child as an offering, so that I might bring them to ruin, so that they would know that I am the LORD.

Offerings on every high hill

27Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and say to them, The Lord GOD says this: In this way too your ancestors insulted me, by breaking faith with me. 28When I brought them into the land I had sworn to give them, wherever they saw a high hill or a leafy tree, they offered their sacrifices there. There they presented offerings that provoked me, there they sent up their soothing aromas, and there they poured out their drink offerings. 29I asked them, “What is this high place you go to?” And it is still called Bamah to this day. 30Therefore say to the house of Israel, The Lord GOD says this: Will you make yourselves unclean as your ancestors did, and prostitute yourselves by running after their vile idols? 31When you offer your gifts and make your children pass through the fire, you are making yourselves unclean with all your idols to this very day. House of Israel, should I then let you consult me? As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you will get no answer from me. 32What you have in mind will never happen, when you say, “We will be like the nations, like the peoples of other lands, who worship wood and stone.” 33As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out, I will rule over you as king. 34I will bring you out from among the peoples and gather you out of the countries where you have been scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out. 35I will lead you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will judge you face to face. 36As I judged your ancestors in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will judge you, declares the Lord GOD. 37I will make you pass under the shepherd’s rod and bring you into the bond of the covenant. 38I will purge from among you those who revolt and rebel against me. I will bring them out of the country where they are living as foreigners, but not one of them will set foot in Israel’s land. Then you will know that I am the LORD. 39As for you, house of Israel, the Lord GOD says this: Go, then, every one of you, and serve your idols, now and later, if you will not listen to me. But you will no longer dishonor my holy name with your gifts and your idols. 40For on my holy mountain, Israel’s high mountain, declares the Lord GOD, there in the land the whole house of Israel, every one of them, will serve me. There I will accept them, and there I will require your contributions and your choicest gifts, with all your holy offerings. 41I will accept you as a soothing aroma when I bring you out from among the peoples and gather you from the countries where you have been scattered, and through you I will show myself holy in the sight of the nations. 42Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I have brought you to the land of Israel, the land I swore to give to your ancestors. 43There you will remember your ways and all the deeds by which you made yourselves unclean, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evil you have done. 44Then you will know that I am the LORD, house of Israel, when I deal with you for the sake of my name and not as your evil ways and your corrupt deeds deserve, declares the Lord GOD.

45The word of the LORD came to me: 46Son of man, turn to face the south. Preach against the south, and prophesy against the forest land of the Negev. 47Say to the forest of the Negev: Hear what the LORD has to say. The Lord GOD says this: I am about to kindle a fire in you, and it will consume every green tree and every dry tree in you. The blazing flame will not be put out, and every face from south to north will be scorched by it. 48Everyone will see that I, the LORD, have set it ablaze; it will not be put out.

Fire in the forest of the south

49Then I said, “Ah, Lord GOD! They are saying about me, ‘Is he not just telling parables?’”
fields.summary: God recounts Israel’s rebellion since Egypt, yet promises to gather them and accept them on God’s holy mountain.

fields.title: Ezekiel 21
fields.body_html:
The sword drawn from its sheath

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, turn to face Jerusalem. Preach against the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel. 3Say to the land of Israel, The LORD says this: I am against you. I will draw my sword out of its sheath and cut off both righteous and wicked from among you. 4Because I will cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked, my sword will come out of its sheath against everyone from south to north. 5Then everyone will know that I, the LORD, have drawn my sword from its sheath; it will not go back again.

6As for you, son of man, groan! Groan before their eyes with a body doubled over and with bitter grief. 7And when they ask you, “Why do you groan?” answer them, “Because of the news, for it is on its way. Every heart will melt, every hand will go limp, every spirit will grow faint, and every knee will be weak as water. It is coming! It will surely happen, declares the Lord GOD.”

The song of the sword

8The word of the LORD came to me:
9Son of man, prophesy and say, The Lord says this:
Say: A sword, a sword, sharpened and polished!
10It is sharpened for slaughter,
polished to flash like lightning.
Or should we rejoice?
The rod of my son despises every tree.
11The sword is handed over for polishing, ready for the hand to grasp;
it is sharpened and polished,
to be put into the hand of the killer.
12Cry out and wail, son of man,
for it is against my people,
against all the princes of Israel.
They are thrown to the sword along with my people.
So strike your thigh in grief.
13For it is a time of testing. And what if even the rod that despises is no more?
declares the Lord GOD.

14So you, son of man, prophesy
and clap your hands.
Let the sword strike twice, even three times, the sword for the slain;
it is the sword for the great slaughter, which closes in on them.
15so that hearts may melt and many may fall.
At all their gates I have set the point of the sword.
Ah! It is made to flash like lightning, drawn for slaughter.
16Slash to the right; turn to the left,
wherever your edge is aimed!
17I too will clap my hands, and I will satisfy my wrath.
I, the LORD, have spoken.

The king of Babylon at the fork in the road

18The word of the LORD came to me: 19As for you, son of man, mark out two roads that the sword of the king of Babylon may take, both of them starting from one country. Carve a signpost, and set it where the road to a city begins. 20Mark one road for the sword to come to Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another to Judah and to Jerusalem, the fortified city. 21For the king of Babylon has stopped at the fork in the road, where the two roads begin, to look for an omen. He shakes the arrows, consults his household gods and examines the liver. 22The omen for Jerusalem falls into his right hand: to set up battering rams, to give the order to kill, to raise the battle cry, to set battering rams against the gates, to heap up a ramp and to build a siege wall. 23To the people of Jerusalem it will seem a false omen, since they have sworn solemn oaths. But he will bring their guilt to mind, and they will be captured.

24Therefore the Lord GOD says this: You have brought your guilt to mind by your open rebellion, so that your sins show in everything you do. Because you have been called to account, you will be taken captive.

A word to the prince of Israel

25As for you, profane and wicked prince of Israel, your day has come, the time of final punishment.

26The Lord GOD says this: Take away the turban and lift off the crown! Things will not stay as they are. Raise up the low and bring down the high. 27A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it! Even this will be no more, until he comes to whom the right belongs, and I will give it to him.

A sword against the Ammonites

28And you, son of man, prophesy and say, The Lord GOD says this about the Ammonites and their taunts. Say: A sword, a sword is drawn for slaughter, polished to devour and to flash like lightning, 29while they see false visions for you and divine lies for you, to lay you on the necks of the slain, the wicked, whose day has arrived, the time of their final punishment. 30Put the sword back in its sheath! Where you were created, in the land of your birth, there I will judge you. 31I will pour out my indignation on you and blow on you with the fire of my wrath. I will hand you over to brutal men, skilled at destroying. 32You will be fuel for the fire, and your blood will be spilled in the land. You will be remembered no more, for I, the LORD, have spoken.
fields.summary: God’s sword is drawn against Jerusalem, and the king of Babylon chooses the road to the city.

fields.title: Ezekiel 22
fields.body_html:
The city of bloodshed

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2As for you, son of man, will you judge? Will you judge the city of bloodshed? Then confront her with all her detestable practices. 3Say, The Lord GOD says this: A city that sheds blood within her walls and so brings on her time of doom, that makes idols for herself and so defiles herself! 4You have become guilty by the blood you have shed, and made unclean by the idols you have made. You have hastened your days and come to the end of your years. So I have made you an object of scorn to the nations and a laughingstock to all the countries. 5Those who are near and those who are far away will mock you, you city with a stained name, full of turmoil. 6Look at the princes of Israel within you: each of them uses his power to shed blood. 7In you, father and mother are treated with contempt; in your midst the foreigner is oppressed; in you the orphan and the widow are wronged. 8You have despised my holy things and dishonored my Sabbaths. 9In you are slanderers who are out to shed blood. In you are those who eat at the mountain shrines. In your midst they commit depraved acts. 10In you men have sexual relations with their father’s wife; in you they violate women who are unclean during their monthly period. 11One man commits a detestable act with his neighbor’s wife; another shamefully defiles his daughter-in-law; and another in you violates his sister, his own father’s daughter. 12In you people take bribes to shed blood. You charge interest and take profit, you make gain from your neighbors by extortion, and you have forgotten me, declares the Lord GOD. 13Look, I strike my hands together at the dishonest gain you have made and at the bloodshed in your midst. 14Will your courage hold, or your hands stay strong, in the days when I take action against you? I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it. 15I will scatter you among the nations, spread you through the countries and burn away your uncleanness. 16Because of your own doing you will be dishonored before the nations. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

Dross in the furnace

17The word of the LORD came to me: 18Son of man, in my sight the house of Israel has become dross. All of them are bronze, tin, iron and lead left in the furnace; they have become the dross from silver.

19Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Because all of you have become dross, I am about to gather you into Jerusalem. 20As silver, bronze, iron, lead and tin are gathered into a furnace and fire is blown on them to melt them, so I will gather you in my anger and my wrath, put you in and melt you. 21I will gather you and blow the fire of my wrath on you, and you will melt inside the city. 22As silver melts in a furnace, so you will melt inside the city. Then you will know that it is I, the LORD, who have poured out my wrath on you.

No one to stand in the gap

23The word of the LORD came to me: 24Son of man, say to the land, You are a land that has not been cleansed, that has had no rain on the day of wrath. 25Her prophets within her have joined in a conspiracy. Like a roaring lion tearing its prey, they devour people; they seize treasure and precious things and make many widows in the land. 26Her priests do violence to my instruction and profane my holy things. They do not separate the holy from the common, and do not teach the difference between the unclean and the clean. They shut their eyes to my Sabbaths, and so I am dishonored among them. 27Her officials within her are like wolves tearing their prey. They shed blood and destroy lives to make dishonest gain. 28Her prophets cover these deeds with whitewash. They see false visions and practice lying divination for them, saying, “The Lord GOD says this,” when the LORD has not spoken. 29The people of the land practice extortion and commit robbery. They wrong the poor and needy and oppress the foreigner, denying them justice. 30I looked for someone among them who would repair the wall and stand before me in the gap on behalf of the land, so that I would not destroy it, but I found no one. 31So I have poured out my indignation on them; I have finished them off with the fire of my wrath and brought their conduct down on their own heads, declares the Lord GOD.
fields.summary: Jerusalem is a city of bloodshed, and God will melt its people in a furnace. Its priests, prophets and princes have all failed.

fields.title: Ezekiel 23
fields.body_html:
Two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, there were two women who were daughters of one mother. 3They prostituted themselves in Egypt; even in their youth they prostituted themselves. There their breasts were fondled, and there men caressed them while they were still virgins. 4The older was named Oholah, and her sister Oholibah. They became mine and bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem. 5While she was still mine, Oholah prostituted herself. She lusted after her lovers, the Assyrians, warriors 6clothed in blue, governors and commanders, all of them handsome young men, horsemen mounted on horses. 7She gave herself as a prostitute to them, to all the elite of Assyria, and she defiled herself with all the idols of everyone she lusted after. 8She did not give up the prostitution she had begun in Egypt, for in her youth men lay with her, fondled her breasts while she was still a virgin and poured out their lust on her. 9So I handed her over to her lovers, the Assyrians she lusted after. 10They stripped her naked, took away her sons and daughters and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, because of the judgments carried out on her.

Oholibah follows her sister

11Her sister Oholibah saw this, yet she was even more depraved in her lust than Oholah, and her prostitution was worse than her sister’s. 12She lusted after the Assyrians, governors and commanders, warriors in splendid dress, horsemen mounted on horses, all of them handsome young men. 13I saw that she had defiled herself; both of them went the same way. 14But she carried her prostitution further. She saw men pictured on a wall, figures of Chaldeans drawn in red, 15with belts around their waists and flowing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like officers, like the Babylonians whose native land is Chaldea. 16The moment her eyes fell on them, she lusted after them, and she sent messengers to them in Chaldea. 17The Babylonians came to her, to the bed of love, and defiled her with their lust. After she had been defiled by them, she turned away from them in disgust. 18When she carried on her prostitution openly and exposed her nakedness, I turned away from her in disgust, as I had turned away from her sister. 19Yet she prostituted herself more and more, remembering the days of her youth when she prostituted herself in the land of Egypt. 20She lusted after her lovers there, men with genitals like a donkey’s and emissions like a stallion’s. 21So you longed for the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians fondled your nipples and your young breasts.

Her lovers turned against her

22Therefore, Oholibah, the Lord GOD says this: I am about to stir up your lovers against you, the ones you turned away from in disgust, and I will bring them upon you from all sides: 23the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa and Koa, together with all the Assyrians, handsome young men, all of them governors and commanders, officers and men of renown, all mounted on horses. 24They will come against you with weapons, chariots and wagons and a horde of peoples. They will take up positions against you on every side with large shields, small shields and helmets. I will hand over judgment to them, and they will judge you by their own standards. 25I will direct my jealous anger against you, and they will treat you with wrath. They will cut off your nose and your ears, and those of you who are left will fall by the sword. They will take your sons and daughters, and what is left of you will be consumed by fire. 26They will strip off your clothes and take away your fine jewelry. 27So I will put an end to your lewdness and to the prostitution you began in the land of Egypt. You will not look to the Egyptians with longing or remember Egypt any more.

28For the Lord GOD says this: I am about to hand you over to those you hate, to those you turned away from in disgust. 29They will deal with you in hatred, take away everything you have worked for and leave you naked and bare. The shame of your prostitution will be exposed, your lewdness and your prostitution. 30This will be done to you because you prostituted yourself with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols. 31You have walked in your sister’s way, so I will put her cup into your hand.

The cup of her sister

32The Lord GOD says this: Your sister’s cup you will drink, deep and wide. It will bring you scorn and mockery, for it holds so much. 33You will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow. It is a cup of horror and ruin, the cup of your sister Samaria. 34You will drink it and drain it dry; you will chew on its broken pieces and tear at your breasts. For I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.

35Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Because you have forgotten me and thrown me behind your back, you must bear the punishment for your lewdness and your prostitution.

Judgment on both sisters

36The LORD said to me: Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? If so, confront them with their detestable practices. 37For they have committed adultery, and there is blood on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols, and they have even offered up to them as food the children they bore to me. 38They have also done this to me: on that same day they defiled my sanctuary and dishonored my Sabbaths. 39After they had slaughtered their children for their idols, they came into my sanctuary that same day and profaned it. That is what they did inside my house! 40They even sent for men to come from far away; a messenger was sent to them, and they came. For them you bathed, painted your eyes and put on your jewelry. 41You sat on a splendid couch with a table laid out in front of it, where you had placed my incense and my oil. 42The noise of a carefree crowd was around her. Along with men from the common people, drunkards were brought in from the desert, and they put bracelets on the women’s arms and beautiful crowns on their heads. 43Then I said of the woman worn out by adulteries, “Even now men will commit prostitution with her!” 44Men went to bed with her as they would with a prostitute; in the same way they went to Oholah and Oholibah, those lewd women. 45But righteous men will sentence them as adulteresses and as women who shed blood are sentenced, because they are adulteresses and there is blood on their hands.

46For the Lord GOD says this: Bring up a crowd against them, and hand them over to terror and plunder. 47The crowd will stone them and hack them down with their swords; their sons and daughters they will kill, and their houses they will set on fire. 48So I will put an end to lewdness in the land, and all women will take warning and not act as lewdly as you did. 49Your lewdness will be repaid on you, and you will bear the penalty for your sins with idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.
fields.summary: Two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah, picture Samaria and Jerusalem in their unfaithfulness, and they will be judged.

fields.title: Ezekiel 24
fields.body_html:
The pot on the fire

1On the tenth day of the tenth month of the ninth year, the word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, write down today’s date, this very date. The king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem on this very day. 3Tell the rebellious house a parable. Say to them, The Lord GOD says this: Put on the pot, put it on, and pour water into it. 4Put the pieces of meat in it, all the good pieces, the thigh and the shoulder; fill it with the choicest bones. 5Take the best of the flock, and pile the bones under the pot. Bring it to a rolling boil, and cook the bones in it.

Woe to the city of bloodshed

6Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Woe to the city of bloodshed, the pot that is crusted with rust, whose rust has not come off! Empty it piece by piece, without casting lots for any of it. 7For the blood she shed is still within her; she spilled it on bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground where dust would cover it. 8To stir up wrath and take vengeance, I have set her blood on bare rock, where it cannot be covered.

9Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Woe to the city of bloodshed! I myself will make the pile of wood high. 10Pile on the logs, light the fire, cook the meat well, mix in the spices, and let the bones be charred. 11Then set the empty pot on the coals until it is hot and its bronze glows, so that its uncleanness melts inside it and its rust is burned away. 12All the effort has been wasted; its thick rust will not come off, not even in the fire. 13Your uncleanness is your lewdness. Because I tried to cleanse you and you would not be clean from your uncleanness, you will not be clean again until I have satisfied my wrath against you. 14I, the LORD, have spoken. The time has come, and I will act. I will not hold back; I will not show pity; I will not change my mind. You will be judged by your ways and your deeds, declares the Lord GOD.

The death of Ezekiel’s wife

15The word of the LORD came to me: 16Son of man, I am about to take away from you the delight of your eyes with one blow. Yet you must not mourn or weep or shed any tears. 17Groan quietly; do not observe mourning for the dead. Keep your turban tied on and your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your upper lip, and do not eat the bread that others bring to mourners. 18So in the morning I spoke to the people, and that evening my wife died. The next morning I did as I had been commanded. 19Then the people asked me, “Will you not tell us what these things you are doing mean for us?” 20I answered them, “The word of the LORD came to me: 21Tell the house of Israel, The Lord GOD says this: I am about to profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes and the desire of your heart. The sons and daughters you left behind will be cut down by the sword. 22Then you will do what I have done. You will not cover your upper lip or eat the bread that others bring to mourners. 23Your turbans will stay on your heads and your sandals on your feet. There will be no mourning or weeping; instead you will waste away because of your guilt and groan to one another. 24Ezekiel will be a sign for you; you will do just as he has done. When it comes, then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.”

A survivor will bring the news

25As for you, son of man, on the day I take from them their stronghold, their joy and glory, the delight of their eyes and the desire of their hearts, and their sons and daughters as well, 26on that day a survivor will come to tell you the news. 27On that day your mouth will be opened to the survivor; you will speak and no longer be silent. So you will become a sign for them. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
fields.summary: A boiling pot pictures Jerusalem’s siege. Ezekiel’s wife dies, and he is told not to mourn, as a sign to the people.

fields.title: Ezekiel 25
fields.body_html:
Against Ammon

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, turn to face the Ammonites and prophesy against them, 3and say to the Ammonites, Hear the word of the Lord GOD! The Lord GOD says this: Because you cried “Aha!” over my sanctuary when it was desecrated, over the land of Israel when it was laid waste, and over the people of Judah when they went into exile, 4therefore I am going to hand you over to the people of the east as their possession. They will set up their camps among you and pitch their tents in your land; they will eat your fruit and drink your milk. 5I will turn Rabbah into a pasture for camels and the land of Ammon into a fold for sheep. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

Ammon’s scorn repaid

6For the Lord GOD says this: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet and gloated with all the scorn in your heart over the land of Israel, 7therefore I have stretched out my hand against you. I will hand you over as plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from among the peoples and wipe you out from among the lands. I will destroy you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

Against Moab

8The Lord GOD says this: Because Moab and Seir said, “See, the people of Judah are just like all the other nations,” 9therefore I am going to lay bare the flank of Moab, stripping it of its cities, the cities on its frontier, the pride of the land: Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon and Kiriathaim. 10I will give it to the people of the east, along with the Ammonites, as their possession, so that the Ammonites will be remembered no more among the nations. 11I will carry out judgments on Moab. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

Against Edom

12The Lord GOD says this: Because Edom took revenge on the people of Judah and became deeply guilty by avenging itself on them, 13therefore the Lord GOD says this: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and wipe out both its people and its animals. I will make it a wasteland; from Teman to Dedan they will fall by the sword. 14I will take my vengeance on Edom through my people Israel. They will deal with Edom as my anger and my wrath demand, and they will know what my vengeance is, declares the Lord GOD.

Against the Philistines

15The Lord GOD says this: Because the Philistines acted in revenge, taking vengeance with scorn in their hearts and seeking to destroy Judah out of their age-old hatred, 16therefore the Lord GOD says this: I am about to stretch out my hand against the Philistines. I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy those who are left along the seacoast. 17I will carry out great acts of vengeance on them and punish them in my wrath. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I take my vengeance on them.
fields.summary: Ezekiel prophesies against Ammon, Moab, Edom and the Philistines.

fields.title: Ezekiel 26
fields.body_html:
Tyre will become a bare rock

1In the eleventh year, on the first day of a month, the word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, because Tyre has said of Jerusalem, “Aha! The gateway of the nations is broken, and its doors have swung open to me. She lies in ruins, and I will grow rich,” 3therefore the Lord GOD says this: I am against you, Tyre. I will bring many nations against you, as the sea hurls up its waves. 4They will destroy the walls of Tyre and pull down her towers. I will scrape away her rubble and make her a bare rock. 5Out in the sea she will become a place where nets are spread to dry, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. She will become the nations’ plunder. 6Her daughter towns on the mainland will be put to the sword. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

Nebuchadrezzar against Tyre

7For the Lord GOD says this: I am bringing against Tyre from the north Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses, chariots and horsemen, a great horde of troops. 8He will put your daughter towns on the mainland to the sword. He will build a siege wall against you, heap up a ramp against you and raise his shields against you. 9He will aim the blows of his battering rams at your walls and tear down your towers with his iron tools. 10His horses will be so many that their dust will cover you. The noise of horsemen, wheels and chariots will make your walls shake when he comes through your gates, as troops pour into a city whose walls are breached. 11His horses’ hooves will trample every street you have. He will kill your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will crash to the ground. 12They will plunder your wealth and seize your goods. They will tear down your walls and demolish your fine houses, and they will throw your stones, timber and rubble into the sea. 13I will silence the noise of your songs, and the music of your lyres will never be heard again. 14I will make you a bare rock, a place for spreading nets. You will never be built again, for I, the LORD, have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.

The princes of the sea mourn

15The Lord GOD says this to Tyre: Will not the coastlands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and the killing goes on within you? 16All the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, lay aside their robes and strip off their embroidered clothes. Trembling will be their clothing. They will sit on the ground, trembling every moment, appalled at your fate.
17They will raise a lament over you and say to you,
“How you have perished, you who were peopled from the seas,
the renowned city that was mighty on the sea, she and those who lived in her,
who spread their terror over all who lived there!
18Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your fall,
and the islands of the sea are dismayed at your passing.”

Down to the pit

19For the Lord GOD says this: When I make you a desolate city, like cities where no one lives, when I bring the deep up over you and its vast waters cover you, 20then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago. I will make you dwell in the world below, among ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will no longer be inhabited. But I will give splendor to the land of the living. 21I will bring you to a terrifying end, and you will be no more. People will look for you, but you will never be found again, declares the Lord GOD.
fields.summary: Tyre will be destroyed by Nebuchadrezzar and never rebuilt.

fields.title: Ezekiel 27
fields.body_html:
A lament for the ship Tyre

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Now you, son of man, raise a lament over Tyre,
3and say to Tyre, the city that sits at the gateways of the sea,
trading with the peoples of many coastlands,
The Lord GOD says this:
Tyre, you have said, “I am perfect in beauty.”
4Your territory is in the heart of the seas;
your builders made your beauty perfect.
5They built all your planks from the junipers of Senir;
a cedar from Lebanon was taken to be your mast.
6They made your oars of oaks from Bashan;
they made your deck of box wood from the coastlands of Kittim, inlaid with ivory.
7Your sail was of fine embroidered linen from Egypt,
and it served as your banner;
your awning was of blue and purple cloth from the coastlands of Elishah.
8Men from Sidon and Arvad were your rowers;
your own skilled men, Tyre, were on board as your sailors.
9The veteran craftsmen of Gebal were on board,
caulking your seams.
All the ships of the sea and their crews came to you
to barter for your goods.
10Men of Persia, Lud and Put served in your army as your warriors.
They hung their shields and helmets in you;
they gave you your splendor.
11Men of Arvad and Helech manned your walls on every side,
and men of Gamad were in your towers.
Their shields hung around your walls;
they made your beauty perfect.
12Tarshish did business with you because of your great wealth of every kind;
they traded silver, iron, tin and lead for your goods.
13Javan, Tubal and Meshech traded with you;
they exchanged slaves and bronze vessels for your goods.
14From Beth-togarmah
they traded horses, war horses and mules for your goods.
15The people of Dedan traded with you;
many coastlands were markets under your control;
they paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
16Aram did business with you because you had so many products;
they gave turquoise, purple cloth, embroidered work, fine linen, coral and rubies for your goods.
17Judah and the land of Israel were your traders;
for your goods they gave wheat from Minnith, millet, honey, oil and balm.
18Damascus did business with you because of your many products and your great wealth of every kind,
trading wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
19Vedan and Javan from Uzal traded for your goods;
wrought iron, cassia and sweet cane were among the goods you bought.
20Dedan traded with you
in saddle blankets for riding.
21Arabia and all the princes of Kedar
were traders under your hand;
in lambs, rams and goats,
in these they did business with you.
22The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you;
they gave the finest of all spices, every kind of precious stone, and gold for your goods.
23Haran, Canneh and Eden, the merchants of Sheba,
Asshur and Chilmad traded with you.
24They traded with you in fine clothing,
in cloaks of blue and embroidered work, and in multicolored carpets
tied with cords and well made, in your market.
25Ships of Tarshish carried your goods;
you were filled with cargo and heavily laden in the heart of the seas.
26Your rowers brought you out onto the mighty waters;
the east wind wrecked you in the heart of the seas.
27Your wealth, your wares and your goods,
your mariners and your sailors,
those who caulk your seams and those who trade your goods, all your warriors on board and all the crew within you,
will sink into the heart of the seas
on the day of your downfall.
28At the sound of your sailors’ cry
the shores will quake.
29All who handle the oar will come down from their ships,
the mariners and all the sailors of the sea;
they will stand on the shore.
30They will raise their voices over you and cry out bitterly.
They will heap dust on their heads
and wallow in ashes.
31They will shave their heads because of you and put on sackcloth.
They will weep over you with anguish of heart and bitter wailing.
32As they wail, they will raise a lament over you and chant over you:
“Who was ever like Tyre,
now silent in the middle of the sea?
33When your goods went out across the seas,
you satisfied many peoples;
with your great wealth and your merchandise
you made the kings of the earth rich.
34Now that you are wrecked by the seas, in the depths of the waters,
your goods and all your crew have sunk with you.
35All who live on the coastlands are appalled at your fate;
their kings shudder with horror,
and their faces are twisted with fear.
36The merchants among the peoples hiss at you;
you have come to a terrifying end,
and you will be no more forever.”
fields.summary: Ezekiel laments for Tyre, pictured as a great ship that sinks in the sea.

fields.title: Ezekiel 28
fields.body_html:
The ruler who said, I am a god

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre, The Lord GOD says this: You are proud at heart, and you have claimed, “I am a god! I sit on the throne of the gods in the heart of the seas.” Yet you are a mortal and not a god, though you count your mind equal to the mind of a god. 3You are indeed wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you! 4By your wisdom and understanding you have won wealth for yourself and filled your treasuries with gold and silver. 5By your great skill in trading you have multiplied your wealth, and your wealth has made your heart proud.

A mortal and not a god

6Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Because you count your mind equal to the mind of a god, 7therefore I am bringing foreigners against you, the most ruthless of nations. They will bare their swords against all that your wisdom made beautiful, and they will defile your splendor. 8They will thrust you down into the pit, and you will be slain and die in the heart of the seas. 9Will you still say, “I am a god,” when you face the one who kills you? You will be only a mortal, not a god, in the hands of those who strike you down. 10At the hands of foreigners you will die the death of the uncircumcised, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.

A lament for the king of Tyre

11Then the word of the LORD came to me:
12Son of man, raise a lament over the king of Tyre
and say to him, The Lord GOD says this:
You were the model of perfection,
full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.
13You were in Eden, the garden of God; you were clothed in every precious stone: carnelian, topaz and emerald, chrysolite, onyx and jasper,
sapphire, turquoise and beryl, and gold.
Your settings and mountings were crafted for you;
on the day you were created they were made ready.
14You were an anointed guardian cherub;
I placed you there. You were on God’s holy mountain;
you walked among the stones of fire.
15You were blameless in your ways
from the day you were created,
until wickedness was found in you.
16Through your vast trade you were filled with violence, and you sinned.
So I threw you in disgrace from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, guardian cherub,
removing you from among the stones of fire.
17Your heart grew proud because of your beauty;
you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor.
I threw you to the ground; I made you a spectacle before kings.
18By your many sins, by the dishonesty of your trade,
you defiled your sanctuaries.
So I brought fire out from within you, and it devoured you;
I turned you to ashes on the ground
in the sight of all who were watching.
19All among the peoples who knew you
are appalled at your fate;
you have come to a terrifying end,
and you will be no more forever.

Against Sidon

20Then the word of the LORD came to me: 21Son of man, turn to face Sidon and prophesy against her, 22and say, The Lord GOD says this: I am against you, Sidon, and I will show my glory within you. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I carry out judgments on her and show myself holy in her. 23I will send plague into her and bloodshed into her streets. The slain will fall within her, struck by the sword that comes against her from every side. Then they will know that I am the LORD. 24The house of Israel will no longer have neighbors who treat them with contempt and hurt them like a pricking brier or a painful thorn. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.

Israel gathered and safe

25The Lord GOD says this: When I gather the house of Israel from the nations where they have been scattered, I will display my holiness among them as the nations look on. Then they will live in their own land, the land I gave to my servant Jacob. 26They will live there in safety; they will build houses and plant vineyards. They will live in safety when I carry out judgments on all their neighbors who despise them. Then they will know that I am the LORD their God.
fields.summary: The king of Tyre, who claims to be a god, will be brought down. Sidon is judged, and Israel will be gathered and live in safety.

fields.title: Ezekiel 29
fields.body_html:
Pharaoh, the great monster of the Nile

1In the tenth month of the tenth year, on its twelfth day, the word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, turn to face Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against the whole of Egypt. 3Speak and say, The Lord GOD says this: I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great monster sprawling in the midst of its streams, who says, “The Nile is mine; I made it for myself.” 4I will put hooks in your jaws and make the fish of your streams stick to your scales. I will drag you up out of your streams, with all the fish of your streams clinging to your scales. 5I will fling you into the desert, you and all the fish of your streams. On the open ground you will fall, and will not be gathered up or collected for burial. I will give you as food to the wild animals and the birds of the sky. 6Then all who live in Egypt will know that I am the LORD. For the house of Israel they were a staff made of reed. 7When they grasped you in their hand, you splintered and tore open all their shoulders; when they leaned on you, you broke and wrenched all their hips.

Egypt laid waste

8Therefore the Lord GOD says this: I am bringing a sword against you, and I will cut off from you both people and animals. 9The land of Egypt will become a desolate ruin. Then they will know that I am the LORD. Because Pharaoh said, “The Nile is mine; I made it,” 10therefore I am against you and against your streams. I will make the land of Egypt a wasteland of ruins and desolation, from Migdol to Syene and on to the border of Cush. 11No human foot will pass through it, and no animal’s foot will cross it; it will stay uninhabited for forty years. 12I will make the land of Egypt desolate among desolate lands, and its cities will lie desolate among ruined cities for forty years. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them among the lands.

A lowly kingdom

13For the Lord GOD says this: When forty years are over, I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered. 14I will restore the fortunes of Egypt and bring them back to Pathros, the land of their origin, and there they will be a lowly kingdom. 15It will be the lowliest of kingdoms and will never again raise itself above the nations. I will make them so small that they will not rule over other nations. 16Egypt will never again be something the house of Israel trusts in. Instead it will remind them of their guilt in turning to Egypt for help. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.

Egypt as Nebuchadrezzar’s wages

17In the first month of the twenty-seventh year, on its first day, the word of the LORD came to me: 18Son of man, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon drove his army to a hard campaign against Tyre. Every head was rubbed bald and every shoulder worn raw. Yet he and his army got nothing from Tyre for all the labor he spent against it.

Pay for his army

19Therefore the Lord GOD says this: I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off its wealth, plunder it and strip it of its spoil, and that will be the pay for his army. 20I have given him the land of Egypt as his pay for the work he did, because they worked for me, declares the Lord GOD.

A horn for Israel

21On that day I will make a horn sprout for the house of Israel, and among them I will open your mouth. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
fields.summary: Ezekiel prophesies against Pharaoh and Egypt, which will be laid waste.

fields.title: Ezekiel 30
fields.body_html:
The day of the LORD on Egypt

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, prophesy and say, The Lord GOD says this: Wail and cry, “Alas for that day!” 3For the day is close; the day of the LORD is close. It will be a cloudy day, a time of reckoning for the nations. 4A sword will come against Egypt, and Cush will be in anguish when the slain fall in Egypt, when its wealth is carried off and its foundations are torn down. 5Cush and Put and Lud, all the foreign peoples, Kub, and the people of the land in covenant with them will fall by the sword along with Egypt.

Egypt’s helpers fall

6The LORD says this: Those who hold Egypt up will fall, and its proud strength will come down. From Migdol to Syene they will fall by the sword within it, declares the Lord GOD. 7They will be desolate among desolate lands, and its cities will lie among ruined cities. 8Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I kindle a fire in Egypt and all its helpers are crushed. 9On that day messengers will set out from me in ships to terrify Cush, which feels secure. Anguish will seize them on the day of Egypt’s doom, for it is surely coming.

By the hand of Babylon

10The Lord GOD says this: By the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon I will bring the hordes of Egypt to an end. 11He and his army with him, the most ruthless of nations, will be brought in to ruin the land. They will bare their swords against Egypt and fill the land with corpses. 12I will dry up the streams of the Nile and sell the land into the power of evil men. By the hand of foreigners I will lay waste the land and everything in it. I, the LORD, have spoken.

Judgment on Egypt’s cities

13The Lord GOD says this: I will destroy the idols and put an end to the worthless gods in Memphis. There will no longer be a prince in the land of Egypt, and I will fill the land of Egypt with fear. 14I will lay Pathros waste, set fire to Zoan and carry out judgments on Thebes. 15I will pour out my wrath on Sin, the fortress of Egypt, and cut off the hordes of Thebes. 16I will set fire to Egypt. Sin will writhe in agony, Thebes will be breached, and Memphis will face enemies in broad daylight. 17The young men of Aven and Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and the cities themselves will go into captivity. 18At Tahpanhes the day will turn dark when I break Egypt’s yoke bars there, and its proud strength will come to an end. A cloud will cover it, and its daughter towns will go into captivity. 19So I will carry out judgments on Egypt. Then they will know that I am the LORD.

Pharaoh’s broken arm

20In the first month of the eleventh year, on its seventh day, the word of the LORD came to me: 21Son of man, I have broken the arm of Egypt’s king, Pharaoh. It has not been bandaged for healing or put in a splint to make it strong enough to hold a sword.

Both arms broken

22Therefore the Lord GOD says this: I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break both his arms, the strong one and the one already broken, and make the sword fall from his hand. 23I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and spread them through the lands. 24I will give strength to the arms of the king of Babylon and place my sword in his hand. But Pharaoh’s arms I will break, and he will groan before him like a man mortally wounded. 25I will make the arms of the king of Babylon strong, but Pharaoh’s arms will drop. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I hand my sword to the king of Babylon and he swings it against the land of Egypt. 26I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and spread them through the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
fields.summary: Egypt’s day of doom is near, and Babylon will strike it.

fields.title: Ezekiel 31
fields.body_html:
A cedar in Lebanon

1In the third month of the eleventh year, on its first day, the word of the LORD came to me:
2Son of man, say to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and to his hordes:
Who can be compared with you in your greatness?
3Consider Assyria, a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches and shade like a forest, towering high,
its top among the clouds.
4The waters made it grow; the deep made it tall,
sending its rivers all around the place where it was planted
and its channels to all the trees of the field.
5So it grew taller
than all the trees of the field.
Its boughs grew many and its branches long because of the abundant water, as it spread its shoots.
6All the birds of the sky nested in its boughs;
under its branches all the wild animals gave birth to their young,
and all the great nations lived in its shade.
7It was beautiful in its greatness, with its long branches,
for its roots went down to abundant waters.
8The cedars in the garden of God could not match it,
the junipers could not equal its boughs,
and the plane trees were nothing like its branches;
no tree in God’s garden was its equal in beauty.
9I made it beautiful
with its many branches,
and all the trees of Eden,
in the garden of God, envied it.

The great tree cut down

10Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Because it grew so tall, setting its top among the clouds, and its heart grew proud of its height, 11I handed it over to the mightiest of the nations, who dealt with it as its wickedness deserved. I drove it out. 12Foreigners from the most ruthless of nations cut it down and left it lying. Its branches fell on the mountains and in every valley, and its boughs lay broken in all the ravines of the land. All the peoples of the earth came out from its shade and left it. 13All the birds of the sky settle on its fallen trunk, and all the wild animals live among its branches. 14This happened so that no other trees by the waters would grow proud of their height or lift their tops among the clouds, and no well-watered tree would rise to such height. For all of them are destined for death, for the world below, among mortals, with those who go down to the pit.

Down to Sheol

15The Lord GOD says this: On the day it went down to Sheol, I made the deep mourn for it and covered it over. I held back its rivers, and its great waters were stopped. I dressed Lebanon in gloom for it, and all the trees of the field wilted because of it. 16I made the nations shake at the sound of its fall, when I brought it down to Sheol with those who go down to the pit. Then in the world below all the trees of Eden took comfort, the choicest and best of Lebanon, every tree that drinks water. 17They too went down with it to Sheol, to those killed by the sword, along with those who were its strength, who had lived in its shade among the nations. 18Which of the trees of Eden was like you in glory and greatness? Yet you too will be brought down with the trees of Eden into the world below. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his hordes, declares the Lord GOD.
fields.summary: Egypt is compared to a great cedar that will be cut down, as Assyria was.

fields.title: Ezekiel 32
fields.body_html:
A lament for Pharaoh

1In the twelfth month of the twelfth year, on its first day, the word of the LORD came to me:
2Son of man, raise a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt
and say to him,
You think of yourself as a lion among the nations,
but you are like a monster in the seas,
thrashing about in your rivers, churning the water with your feet
and muddying the streams.
3The Lord GOD says this:
I will throw my net over you
with a throng of many peoples,
and they will drag you up in my net.
4I will leave you on the land
and fling you onto the open field.
I will let all the birds of the sky settle on you
and let the wild animals of the whole earth gorge themselves on you.
5I will spread your flesh on the mountains
and fill the valleys with your carcass.
6I will drench the land with your flowing blood all the way to the mountains,
and the ravines will be full of you.
7When I snuff you out, I will veil the heavens
and make their stars go dark.
I will wrap the sun in a cloud,
and the moon will give no light.
8All the bright lights of the heavens
I will turn dark above you,
and I will bring darkness over your land,
declares the Lord GOD.
9I will trouble
the hearts of many peoples
when I bring news of your destruction among the nations,
to lands you have never known.
10I will make many peoples appalled at you, and their kings will shudder with horror over you
when I brandish my sword before them.
They will tremble every moment, each one for his own life,
on the day of your fall.

The sword of Babylon

11For the Lord GOD says this:
The sword of the king of Babylon will come against you.
12I will make your hordes fall by the swords of warriors,
all of them the most ruthless of nations.
They will shatter the pride of Egypt,
and all its hordes will be destroyed.
13I will destroy all its cattle
beside the abundant waters.
No human foot will churn them again,
and no hooves of cattle will muddy them.
14Then I will let their waters settle
and make their rivers flow smooth as oil,
declares the Lord GOD.
15When I make the land of Egypt desolate and strip the land of all that fills it,
when I strike down everyone living in it,
then they will know that I am the LORD.
16This is a lament, and it will be chanted;
the women of the nations will chant it.
Over Egypt and all its hordes they will chant it,
declares the Lord GOD.

Egypt among the fallen

17It was the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, when the word of the LORD came to me: 18Son of man, wail for the hordes of Egypt and send them down, Egypt and the daughters of mighty nations, to the world below, with those who go down to the pit. 19Are you lovelier than anyone else? Go down and be laid to rest with the uncircumcised! 20They will fall among those killed by the sword. The sword is ready; Egypt is dragged away with all her hordes. 21From the depths of Sheol the mightiest of warriors will speak to Pharaoh and his allies: “They have come down; they lie among the uncircumcised, killed by the sword.” 22Assyria is there with all its company, its graves all around it, all of them slain, fallen by the sword. 23Their graves are set in the deepest parts of the pit, and its company lies around its grave. All of them were slain, fallen by the sword, who once filled the land of the living with terror. 24Elam is there, with all its hordes around its grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword. They went down uncircumcised to the world below, those who spread their terror in the land of the living. Now they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit. 25Among the slain a bed has been made for Elam with all its hordes, their graves around it, all of them uncircumcised, killed by the sword. Because their terror was spread in the land of the living, they now carry their disgrace with those who go down to the pit; they are laid among the slain. 26Meshech and Tubal are there, with all their hordes, their graves around them, all of them uncircumcised, killed by the sword, because they once made the land of the living fear them. 27They do not lie with the fallen warriors of the uncircumcised, who went down to Sheol armed for war, their swords laid under their heads and their guilt resting on their bones, though the terror of these warriors was in the land of the living. 28And you too, Pharaoh, will be broken among the uncircumcised and lie with those killed by the sword. 29Edom is there, its kings and all its princes, who for all their might are laid with those killed by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised, with those who go down to the pit. 30All the chiefs of the north are there, and all the Sidonians. They went down with the slain, put to shame for all the terror their might once caused. They lie uncircumcised with those killed by the sword and bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit. 31Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his hordes, Pharaoh and all his army, killed by the sword, declares the Lord GOD. 32For I spread my terror in the land of the living. So Pharaoh and all his hordes will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.
fields.summary: Ezekiel laments for Pharaoh, who will go down to the grave with the uncircumcised.

fields.title: Ezekiel 33
fields.body_html:
The watchman’s duty

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, speak to your own people and say to them, Suppose I bring the sword on some land, and its people pick one of their number and make him their watchman, 3and he sees the sword coming against the land and blows the ram’s horn to warn the people. 4If anyone hears the sound of the horn but does not take the warning, and the sword comes and takes them away, their blood will be on their own head. 5They heard the sound of the horn but did not take the warning, so their blood will be on them. If they had taken the warning, they would have saved their life. 6But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the horn, so that the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes the life of any one of them, that person is taken away for their sin, but I will hold the watchman responsible for their death.

Ezekiel is appointed watchman again

7As for you, son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel. When you hear a word from my mouth, you must warn them for me. 8If I say to a wicked person, “Wicked one, you will surely die,” and you do not speak out to turn them from their way, that wicked person will die for their sin, but I will hold you responsible for their death. 9But if you warn the wicked to turn from their way, and they do not turn from it, they will die for their sin, but you will have saved yourself.

Turn back and live

10As for you, son of man, say to the house of Israel, This is what you have been saying: “Our rebellious acts and our sins weigh on us, and we are wasting away because of them. How then can we live?” 11Tell them, As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, the death of the wicked gives me no pleasure. I would rather that they turn from their ways and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why would you die, house of Israel?

Each person judged by their own ways

12As for you, son of man, say to your own people, The righteousness of righteous people will not save them when they rebel. And the wickedness of wicked people will not bring them down when they turn from their wickedness. Righteous people will not be able to live by their righteousness when they sin. 13If I say that righteous people will surely live, but they trust in their own righteousness and do wrong, none of the righteous things they have done will be remembered. Because of the wrong they have done, they will die. 14Again, if I say to wicked people, “You will surely die,” but they turn from their sin and do what is just and right, 15if they return what was given them as a pledge, pay back what they have taken by robbery, and follow the statutes that give life, doing nothing wrong, they will surely live; they will not die. 16None of the sins they have committed will be remembered against them. They have done what is just and right; they will surely live. 17Yet your own people say, “The Lord’s way is not fair.” But it is their own way that is not fair. 18If righteous people turn away from their righteousness and do wrong, they will die for it. 19And if wicked people turn away from their wickedness and do what is just and right, they will live because of it. 20Yet you say, “The Lord’s way is not fair.” House of Israel, I will judge each of you according to your ways. 21In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, a survivor who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me and said, “The city has fallen!” 22The evening before the survivor arrived, the hand of the LORD had come on me, and he had opened my mouth by the time the man reached me the next morning. My mouth was opened, and I was silent no more.

The claim of those left in the ruins

23The word of the LORD came to me: 24Son of man, the people who live among those ruins in Israel keep saying, “Abraham was just one man, and yet the land became his. But there are many of us. The land has surely been given to us to possess.”

25Therefore say to them, The Lord GOD says this: You eat meat with the blood still in it, look to your idols and shed blood. And you expect to possess the land? 26You rely on your sword, you do detestable things, and each of you defiles his neighbor’s wife. And you expect to possess the land?

27Say this to them: The Lord GOD says this: As surely as I live, those who are in the ruins will fall by the sword, whoever is out in the open field I will give to the wild animals to be eaten, and those in the strongholds and caves will die of plague. 28I will make the land a desolate waste, and the strength it was so proud of will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will be so desolate that no one will travel through them. 29Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I make the land a desolate waste because of all the detestable things they have done.

Hearers who do not act

30As for you, son of man, your own people are talking about you beside the walls and in the doorways of their houses. They say to one another, “Come and hear what message has come from the LORD.” 31They come to you as people usually do and sit in front of you as if they were my people. They hear your words, but they do not put them into practice. With their mouths they speak of love, but their hearts are set on gain. 32To them you are like someone who sings love songs with a beautiful voice and plays an instrument well. They hear your words, but they do not put them into practice. 33But when all this comes true, and it surely will, they will know that a prophet has been among them.
fields.summary: God makes Ezekiel a watchman again and calls the wicked to turn and live. News comes that Jerusalem has fallen.

fields.title: Ezekiel 34
fields.body_html:
The shepherds who fed themselves

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s shepherds. Prophesy, and tell those shepherds, The Lord GOD says this: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who have been taking care of themselves! Should not shepherds take care of the flock? 3You eat the fat, you dress in the wool, and you slaughter the best animals, but you do not take care of the flock. 4You have not strengthened the weak or healed the sick or bandaged the injured. You have not brought back the strays or gone looking for the lost. You have ruled them with force and cruelty instead. 5So they were scattered because there was no shepherd, and when they were scattered they became food for every wild animal. 6My sheep wandered over all the mountains and on every high hill. My flock was scattered over the whole earth, and no one searched or looked for them. 7Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD: 8As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because my flock has become prey and food for every wild animal, since there was no shepherd, and because my shepherds did not search for my flock but took care of themselves instead of my flock,

9therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD: 10The Lord GOD says this: I am against the shepherds, and I will hold them accountable for my flock. I will remove them from tending the flock, so that the shepherds can no longer feed themselves. I will rescue my flock from their mouths, and the sheep will no longer be food for them.

The LORD will shepherd his flock

11For the Lord GOD says this: I myself will search for my flock and look after them. 12As a shepherd looks after his flock when he is among his scattered sheep, so I will look after my flock. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of clouds and thick darkness. 13I will lead them out from among the peoples, gather them from the lands and bring them home to their own soil. On the mountains of Israel I will feed them, in the ravines and in every settled place in the land. 14I will feed them in good pasture, and their grazing land will be on the high mountains of Israel. There they will lie down in good grazing land and feed on rich pasture on the mountains of Israel. 15I myself will take care of my flock and let them lie down in rest, declares the Lord GOD. 16I will search for the lost and bring back the strays. I will bandage the injured and strengthen the sick, but the fat and strong ones I will destroy. I will tend the flock with justice. 17As for you, my flock, the Lord GOD says this: I will judge between one sheep and another, between rams and male goats. 18Is it not enough for you to graze on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of your pasture underfoot? Is it not enough that you drink clear water? Must you also stir up the rest with your feet and make it muddy? 19And my flock must eat what you have trampled with your feet and drink what you have muddied with your feet.

Judgment between sheep and sheep

20Therefore the Lord GOD says this to them: I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the thin sheep. 21Because you shove with flank and shoulder and butt all the weak with your horns until you have driven them away, 22I will save my flock, and they will no longer be plundered. I will judge between one sheep and another. 23I will set over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he will take care of them. He will tend them and be their shepherd. 24I, the LORD, will be their God, and among them my servant David will be prince. I, the LORD, have spoken. 25I will make a covenant of peace with them and rid the land of wild animals, so that they can live safely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods. 26I will make them a blessing, and the places around my hill as well. I will send down rain when it is due; there will be showers of blessing. 27The trees of the field will bear their fruit and the land will give its harvest, and they will live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the power of those who made them slaves. 28They will no longer be plundered by the nations, and the wild animals will not devour them. They will live in safety, and no one will make them afraid. 29I will provide for them a land famous for its crops, and they will no longer be wasted by famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations. 30Then they will know that I, the LORD their God, am present with them, and that the house of Israel is my people, declares the Lord GOD. 31You are my flock, the sheep of my pasture. You are mortals, and I am your God, declares the Lord GOD.
fields.summary: God condemns the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves, and promises to shepherd the flock and set David over them.

fields.title: Ezekiel 35
fields.body_html:
A message against Mount Seir

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, turn to face Mount Seir and prophesy against it. 3Say to it, The Lord GOD says this: I am against you, Mount Seir. I will raise my hand against you and turn you into a desolate waste. 4I will lay your towns in ruins, and you will be laid waste. Then you will know that I am the LORD. 5Because you kept up an age-old hostility and handed the Israelites over to the sword at the time of their disaster, the time when their punishment reached its end, 6therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will hand you over to bloodshed, and bloodshed will pursue you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will pursue you. 7I will make Mount Seir a desolate ruin and cut off from it everyone who comes and goes. 8I will fill its mountains with the dead.
