Those killed by the sword will fall on your hills and in your valleys and all your ravines. 9I will make you desolate forever, and your towns will not be lived in again. Then you will know that I am the LORD. 10Because you said, “Both nations and both countries will be mine; we will take them over,” even though the LORD was there, 11therefore, as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will treat you with the same anger and envy that you showed in your hatred of them, and when I judge you, I will make myself known among them. 12Then you will know that I am the LORD. I have heard all the insults you spoke against the mountains of Israel when you said, “They lie desolate; they have been handed to us to devour.” 13You boasted against me with your mouths and piled up words against me. I heard it all.

14The Lord GOD says this: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate. 15Just as you rejoiced when the house of Israel’s inheritance became desolate, I will do the same to you. You will be desolate, Mount Seir, you and all Edom, every part of it. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
fields.summary: God will judge Mount Seir, Edom, for its hostility toward Israel.

fields.title: Ezekiel 36
fields.body_html:
Hope for the mountains of Israel

1Now, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel. Say, Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD. 2The Lord GOD says this: The enemy said about you, “Aha! The ancient heights have become our property!” 3Therefore prophesy and say, The Lord GOD says this: They made you desolate and hounded you from every side, so that you became the property of the rest of the nations, and people talked and gossiped about you. 4therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD. The Lord GOD says this to the mountains and hills, the ravines and valleys, the desolate ruins and the abandoned towns that have been plundered and mocked by the rest of the nations around them.

5therefore the Lord GOD says this: In the fire of my jealousy I have spoken out against the other nations and against all of Edom. With hearts full of glee and with utter contempt, they took my land for themselves, so that they could plunder its pastures. 6Therefore prophesy about the land of Israel and say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, The Lord GOD says this: I have spoken in my jealousy and my wrath, because you have suffered the scorn of the nations. 7Therefore the Lord GOD says this: I have raised my hand in an oath that the nations around you will themselves suffer scorn. 8But you, mountains of Israel, will put out your branches and produce your fruit for my people Israel, because they will soon come home. 9For I am on your side, and I will turn to you with favor. You will be plowed and planted. 10I will multiply the people living on you, the whole house of Israel, every one of them. The towns will be lived in, and the ruins rebuilt. 11I will multiply people and animals on you, and they will increase and be fruitful. I will settle people on you as in the past, and I will make you more prosperous than you were at first. Then you will know that I am the LORD. 12I will lead people to walk on you again, my people Israel. They will take possession of you, and you will be their heritage. You will never again rob them of their children.

13The Lord GOD says this: People say about you, “You devour people, and you rob your nation of its children.” 14Therefore you will no longer devour people or rob your nation of its children, declares the Lord GOD. 15I will no longer let you hear the nations’ insults, and you will no longer bear the scorn of the peoples or make your nation fall, declares the Lord GOD.

For the sake of his holy name

16The word of the LORD came to me: 17Son of man, while the house of Israel was living in its own land, they made it unclean by their conduct and deeds. To me their conduct was like the impurity of a woman during her period. 18So I poured out my wrath on them because of the blood they had shed in the land and because they had defiled it with their idols. 19I scattered them among the nations and dispersed them through the lands. I judged them by their conduct and their deeds. 20Among the nations they came to, they profaned my holy name, for people said of them, “These are the people of the LORD, and yet they had to leave his land.” 21But I was concerned for my holy name, the name the house of Israel profaned in the nations they went to.

A new heart and a new spirit

22Therefore say to the house of Israel, The Lord GOD says this: I am not about to act for your sake, house of Israel, but for the sake of my holy name, which you have profaned in the nations you went to. 23I will show that my great name is holy, the name that has been dishonored among the nations, which you dishonored among them. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD, as I display my holiness through you before their eyes. 24I will take you out of the nations, gather you from every land and bring you back to your own country. 25I will sprinkle pure water over you, and you will be clean. From all your impurities and from all your idols I will make you clean. 26I will give you a new heart, and I will place a new spirit within you. I will take the heart of stone out of your bodies and give you a heart of flesh. 27I will put my Spirit within you and make you follow my statutes and carefully keep my rulings. 28You will live in the land I gave to your ancestors. You will be my people, and I will be your God. 29I will save you from all your impurities. I will call for the grain and make it abundant, and I will not send famine on you. 30I will make the fruit trees and the fields produce plenty, so that you will never again suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations. 31Then you will call to mind your evil ways and the things you did that were not good, and you will be disgusted with yourselves for your guilt and your detestable practices. 32I am not about to act for your sake, declares the Lord GOD. Be sure of that! Be ashamed and humiliated because of your conduct, house of Israel.

Like the garden of Eden

33The Lord GOD says this: On the day I cleanse you from all your sins, I will cause the towns to be lived in, and the ruins will be rebuilt. 34The land that lay desolate will be farmed again, instead of lying waste for every passerby to see. 35People will say, “This land that was laid waste has become like the garden of Eden. The towns that lay ruined, desolate and torn down are now walled and lived in.” 36Then the nations still left around you will know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt the ruins and replanted the wasteland. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.

37The Lord GOD says this: This too I will let the house of Israel ask of me, and I will do it for them: I will make their people as many as a flock of sheep. 38Like the flocks brought as holy offerings, like the flocks in Jerusalem at her appointed festivals, so the ruined towns will be crowded with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
fields.summary: The mountains of Israel will be fruitful again. God will give the people a new heart and a new spirit for the sake of God’s holy name.

fields.title: Ezekiel 37
fields.body_html:
The valley of dry bones

1The hand of the LORD came on me, and he carried me out by the Spirit of the LORD and put me down in the middle of the valley. It was full of bones. 2He led me back and forth among them, and I saw that there were a great many of them on the floor of the valley, and they were very dry. 3He asked me, “Son of man, can these bones live?” I answered, “Lord GOD, only you know.” 4Then he said to me, “Prophesy over these bones and say to them, Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD! 5The Lord GOD says this to these bones: I am going to put breath into you, and you will come to life. 6I will put tendons on you and make flesh grow on you and cover you with skin. I will put breath in you, and you will come alive. Then you will know that I am the LORD.” 7So I prophesied as I had been told. While I was prophesying, there was a noise, a rattling sound, and the bones came together, each bone to its own bone. 8As I watched, tendons appeared on them, flesh grew on them, and skin covered them over. But there was no breath in them. 9Then he told me, “Prophesy to the breath. Prophesy, son of man, and say to it, The Lord GOD says this: Come from the four winds, breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live.” 10So I prophesied as he had commanded me, and breath entered them. They came to life and stood up on their feet, a huge army.

11He said to me, “Son of man, these bones stand for the whole house of Israel. They keep saying, ‘Our bones have dried up, our hope is gone; we are completely cut off.’ 12So prophesy and say to them, The Lord GOD says this: I am going to open your graves and raise you up out of them, my people. I will bring you into the land of Israel.

13Then you will know that I am the LORD, my people, when I open your graves and raise you up out of them. 14I will put my Spirit within you so that you live, and I will set you down on your own soil. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken and will act, declares the LORD.”

Two sticks become one

15The word of the LORD came to me: 16Now you, son of man, take a stick of wood and inscribe it, “For Judah and the Israelites allied with him.” Then take a second stick and inscribe it, “For Joseph, that is, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel allied with him.” 17Join the two to each other to make one stick, so that they are one in your hand. 18When your own people ask you, “Will you not tell us what you mean by this?” 19tell them, The Lord GOD says this: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim’s hand, and of the tribes of Israel associated with him, and join it to the stick of Judah. I will make them a single stick, and they will become one in my hand. 20Hold the sticks you have written on in your hand where they can see them, 21and say to them, The Lord GOD says this: I am going to take the Israelites out of the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from all around and bring them back to their own land. 22I will make them into a single nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, with one king ruling over them all. Never again will they be two nations or be split into two kingdoms. 23They will no longer make themselves unclean with their idols, their vile idols or any of their rebellious acts. I will rescue them from all the places where they lived and sinned, and I will make them clean. They will be my people, and I will be their God. 24My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow my rulings and be careful to keep my statutes. 25They will live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob, the land where your ancestors lived. They will live there forever, they and their children and their grandchildren, and my servant David will be their prince forever. 26I will make a covenant of peace with them, a covenant that will last forever. I will establish them and make them numerous, and I will place my sanctuary among them forever. 27My dwelling place will be among them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people. 28Then the nations will know that I, the LORD, make Israel holy, when my sanctuary is among them forever.
fields.summary: In the valley of dry bones God tells Ezekiel to prophesy, and the bones come together and live. Two sticks joined together picture Judah and Israel united under one king.

fields.title: Ezekiel 38
fields.body_html:
Gog comes from the north

1The word of the LORD came to me: 2Son of man, turn to face Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, from the land of Magog, and prophesy against him. 3Say, The Lord GOD says this: I am against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. 4I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws and lead you out with all your army, your horses and your horsemen, every one of them fully armed, a great company with shields large and small, all of them carrying swords. 5Persia, Cush and Put are with them, all with shield and helmet. 6Gomer with all its troops, and Beth-togarmah from the farthest north with all its troops. Many peoples are with you. 7Get ready and be prepared, you and all the forces gathered around you, and take command of them. 8After many days you will be called up. In the latter years you will invade a land that has recovered from war, whose people have been brought together out of many nations onto the mountains of Israel, which had lain in ruins for a long time. They were brought out from the nations, and now they all live in safety. 9You will advance like a storm and come like a cloud covering the land, you and all your troops and the many peoples with you.

Gog’s evil plan

10The Lord GOD says this: On that day thoughts will rise in your mind, and you will make a wicked plan. 11You will say, “I will attack a land of unwalled villages. I will come against a peaceful people living in safety, all of them living without walls, with no bars or gates,” 12in order to seize plunder and loot, to turn your hand against the resettled ruins and against the people gathered from the nations, who have gained livestock and goods and who live at the center of the world. 13Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish with all its young lions will ask you, “Have you come to take plunder? Have you gathered your army to carry off loot, to take away silver and gold, livestock and goods, and to seize a great haul?”

14Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog, The Lord GOD says this: On that day, when my people Israel are living in safety, will you not take notice? 15You will come from your home in the far north, you and many nations with you, all of them on horseback, a great horde and a mighty army. 16Like a cloud covering the land, you will advance on my people Israel. In the latter days I will bring you against my land, Gog, so that the nations come to know me when through you I show myself holy before their eyes.

The LORD shows his greatness

17The Lord GOD says this: Are you not the one I spoke about in days long past through my servants the prophets of Israel? In those days they prophesied for years that I would bring you against them.

18But on that day, when Gog attacks the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, my wrath will blaze up in my anger. 19In my jealousy and in my blazing wrath I declare that a great earthquake will strike the land of Israel on that day. 20The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the wild animals, every creature that creeps along the ground, and all the people on the face of the earth will quake before my. The mountains will be overturned, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will crumble to the ground. 21On all my mountains I will call for a sword against Gog, declares the Lord GOD. Every soldier’s sword will be turned against his comrade. 22I will bring him to judgment with plague and bloodshed. I will pour down on him, on his troops and on the many peoples with him torrents of rain, hailstones, fire and burning sulfur. 23So I will show myself great and holy, and I will make myself known before many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
fields.summary: Gog of the land of Magog will attack the restored Israel, but God will defeat him.

fields.title: Ezekiel 39
fields.body_html:
Gog’s defeat

1As for you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say, The Lord GOD says this: I am against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. 2I will turn you around and drive you along. I will bring you up from the far north and lead you against the mountains of Israel. 3Then I will knock the bow from your left hand and make the arrows drop from your right hand. 4On Israel’s mountains you will fall, you and all your troops and the peoples with you. I will give you as food to birds of prey of every sort and to the wild animals. 5You will fall out in the open, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. 6I will send fire on Magog and on those who live in safety in the coastlands. Then they will know that I am the LORD. 7Among my people Israel I will make my holy name known, and I will no longer let my holy name be profaned. Then the nations will know that I, the LORD, am the Holy One in Israel. 8It is coming! It will certainly take place, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day I have spoken of. 9Then the people living in the towns of Israel will go out and use the weapons for fuel, burning shields large and small, bows and arrows, war clubs and spears. For seven years they will use them to make fires. 10They will not need to gather wood from the fields or cut it from the forests, because they will burn the weapons for fuel. They will plunder those who plundered them and loot those who looted them, declares the Lord GOD.

The burial of Gog’s army

11On that day I will give Gog a burial ground in Israel, the valley of the Travelers east of the sea, and it will block the way of those who travel through. There they will bury Gog and all his horde, and it will be called the valley of Hamon-gog. 12The house of Israel will spend seven months burying them, to make the land clean. 13All the people of the land will take part in the burying, and it will bring them honor on the day I display my glory, declares the Lord GOD. 14They will appoint men to work full time going through the land, and with them others to bury the bodies left lying on the ground, so as to cleanse it. At the end of the seven months they will begin a search. 15As they go through the land, whenever one of them sees a human bone, he will set up a marker beside it so that the gravediggers can bury it in the valley of Hamon-gog. 16A town there will also be named Hamonah. So they will cleanse the land.

The feast for the birds and beasts

17As for you, son of man, the Lord GOD says this: Call out to every kind of bird and to all the wild animals: Assemble and come! Gather from all around to the sacrifice I am preparing for you, a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel, where you will eat flesh and drink blood. 18You will eat the flesh of mighty men and drink the blood of the rulers of the earth as if they were rams and lambs, goats and bulls, all of them fattened animals from Bashan. 19At the sacrifice I am preparing for you, you will eat fat till you are full and drink blood till you are drunk. 20At my table you will be filled with horses and charioteers, with mighty men and every kind of soldier, declares the Lord GOD. 21I will display my glory among the nations. Every nation will see the judgment I carry out and the power I use against them. 22The house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God from that day on. 23The nations will come to understand that the house of Israel was exiled because of its guilt, because it broke faith with me. So I hid my face from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword. 24I dealt with them as their impurity and their rebellious acts deserved, and I hid my face from them.

The LORD will restore Israel

25Therefore the Lord GOD says this: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and show compassion to the whole house of Israel, and I will be zealous for my holy name. 26They will bear their shame and all the unfaithfulness they showed toward me, when they live in safety in their own land with no one to frighten them, 27when I have brought them home from the peoples and gathered them from the lands of their enemies, and shown myself holy through them before many nations. 28Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, who sent them into exile among the nations and then gathered them back into their own land, leaving none of them behind. 29Never again will I hide my face from them, because I will pour out my Spirit upon the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.
fields.summary: Gog’s armies fall, and Israel spends months burying the dead. God will pour out the Spirit on Israel.

fields.title: Ezekiel 40
fields.body_html:
The vision of the new temple

1On the tenth day of the month at the start of the year, in the twenty-fifth year of our exile, the fourteenth year after the city had fallen, on that very day the hand of the LORD came on me, and he brought me there. 2In visions from God he brought me to the land of Israel and placed me on a very high mountain. On it, toward the south, was something like the buildings of a city. 3When he brought me there, I saw a man who looked like bronze. He had a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand, and he was standing in the gateway. 4The man said to me, “Son of man, look carefully, listen closely, and give your mind to everything I will show you. You were brought here so that I could show it to you. Tell the house of Israel everything you see.” 5There was a wall all around the outside of the temple area. The measuring reed in the man’s hand was about 10 1/2 feet long; each of its six cubits was a cubit and a handbreadth. He measured the wall, and it was about 10 1/2 feet thick and about 10 1/2 feet high. 6Then he went to the gate that faces east. He climbed its steps and measured the threshold of the gate: it was about 10 1/2 feet deep. The other threshold was also about 10 1/2 feet deep. 7Each alcove was about 10 1/2 feet long and about 10 1/2 feet wide, and the walls between the alcoves were about 8 3/4 feet thick. The threshold of the gate next to the porch of the gate, on the inner side, was about 10 1/2 feet deep. 8He measured the porch of the gate on the inner side: it was about 10 1/2 feet. 9Then he measured the porch of the gate: it was about 14 feet deep, and its jambs were about 3 1/2 feet thick. The porch of the gate faced the temple. 10The east gate had three alcoves on each side. All three were the same size, and the jambs on each side were the same size. 11He measured the width of the gate’s entrance: it was about 17 1/2 feet; and the gateway was about 22 3/4 feet long. 12In front of the alcoves was a barrier about 21 inches high on each side, and the alcoves were about 10 1/2 feet square on each side. 13He measured the gate from the roof of one alcove to the roof of the alcove opposite: the width was about 43 3/4 feet, from one opening to the opening facing it. 14He also measured the jambs: about 105 feet. The gate reached to the jamb of the court on every side. 15From the front of the gate at the entrance to the far end of the porch on the inner side was about 87 1/2 feet. 16The alcoves and their jambs had recessed windows facing the inside of the gate all around, and so did the porch. There were windows all around on the inside, and the jambs were decorated with palm trees. 17Then he brought me into the outer court. There were rooms there, and a pavement laid all around the court; thirty rooms faced the pavement. 18The pavement ran along the sides of the gates and was as wide as the gates were long. This was the lower pavement. 19He measured the distance from the inner front of the lower gate to the outer front of the inner court: it was about 175 feet, on the east side and on the north. 20Next he measured the length and the width of the gate of the outer court that faces north. 21Its alcoves, three on each side, its jambs and its porch had the same measurements as the first gate. It was about 87 1/2 feet long and about 43 3/4 feet wide. 22Its windows, its porch and its palm trees had the same measurements as those of the gate that faces east. Seven steps led up to it, and its porch was at the inner end. 23The inner court had a gate opposite the north gate, as it had on the east. He measured from gate to gate: about 175 feet. 24Then he led me to the south side, and there was a gate facing south. He measured its jambs and its porch, and they had the same measurements as the others. 25The gate and its porch had windows all around like the other windows. It was about 87 1/2 feet long and about 43 3/4 feet wide. 26Seven steps led up to it, and its porch was at the inner end. It had palm trees on its jambs, one on each side. 27The inner court also had a gate facing south. He measured from this gate to the outer gate on the south: about 175 feet. 28Then he brought me into the inner court through the south gate. He measured the south gate, and it had the same measurements as the others. 29Its alcoves, its jambs and its porch had the same measurements as the others, and the gate and its porch had windows all around. It was about 87 1/2 feet long and about 43 3/4 feet wide. 30There were porches all around, about 43 3/4 feet long and about 8 3/4 feet wide. 31Its porch faced the outer court, and its jambs were decorated with palm trees. Eight steps led up to it. 32Then he brought me to the inner court on the east side. He measured the gate, and it had the same measurements as the others. 33Its alcoves, its jambs and its porch had the same measurements as the others, and the gate and its porch had windows all around. It was about 87 1/2 feet long and about 43 3/4 feet wide. 34Its porch faced the outer court, and its jambs on both sides were decorated with palm trees. Eight steps led up to it. 35Next he brought me to the north gate and measured it; its measurements matched the others, 36with its alcoves, its jambs and its porch, and it had windows all around. It was about 87 1/2 feet long and about 43 3/4 feet wide. 37Its jambs faced the outer court, and its jambs on both sides were decorated with palm trees. Eight steps led up to it. 38There was a room with its door by the jambs of the gate, where the burnt offering was washed. 39In the porch of the gate there were two tables on each side, on which the burnt offerings, the sin offerings and the guilt offerings were to be slaughtered. 40Outside, as one went up to the entrance of the north gate, two tables stood on one side, and two more stood on the other side of the gate’s porch. 41So there were four tables on each side of the gate, eight tables in all, on which the animals were slaughtered. 42There were also four tables of cut stone for the burnt offering, about 31 1/2 inches long, about 31 1/2 inches wide and about 21 inches high. On them were placed the tools used for slaughtering the burnt offerings and the other sacrifices. 43Hooks about 3 inches long were fixed all around inside the room, and the meat of the offerings was laid on the tables. 44Outside the inner gate, within the inner court, were rooms for the singers. One was beside the north gate, facing south, and one was beside the east gate, facing north. 45He said to me, “This room facing south is for the priests who are in charge of the temple, 46and the room facing north is for the priests who are in charge of the altar. These are the descendants of Zadok, the only ones among the descendants of Levi who may come near to the LORD to serve him.” 47Then he measured the court. It was square, about 175 feet long and about 175 feet wide. The altar stood in front of the temple. 48Then he brought me to the porch of the temple and measured its jambs: they were about 8 3/4 feet on each side. The sides of the entrance were about 5 1/4 feet wide on each side. 49The porch was about 35 feet wide and about 19 1/4 feet deep, and steps led up to it. There were pillars beside the jambs, one on each side.
fields.summary: In a vision Ezekiel is taken to a high mountain and sees a man with a measuring rod measuring a new temple.

fields.title: Ezekiel 41
fields.body_html:
The temple building

1Then he brought me into the main hall of the temple and measured the jambs. They were about 10 1/2 feet thick on each side, the width of the tent. 2The entrance was about 17 1/2 feet wide, and the walls on either side of it were about 8 3/4 feet wide. He measured the main hall: it was about 70 feet long and about 35 feet wide. 3Then he went into the inner room and measured the jambs of its entrance: they were about 3 1/2 feet thick. The entrance was about 10 1/2 feet wide, and its side walls were about 12 1/4 feet wide. 4He measured the room beyond the main hall: it was about 35 feet long and about 35 feet wide. He said to me, “This is the most holy place.” 5Then he measured the wall of the temple: it was about 10 1/2 feet thick. The side rooms all around the temple were each about 7 feet wide. 6The side rooms were in three stories, one above another, thirty on each story. The wall of the temple had ledges all around to hold up the side rooms, so that their beams did not have to be set into the wall of the temple itself. 7The side rooms became wider at each story going up, because the structure surrounding the temple went up in stages all around it. So the building became wider toward the top, and one went up from the lowest story to the top story through the middle one. 8I saw that the temple had a raised platform all around it. The foundations of the side rooms were a full reed, about 10 1/2 feet, to the joint. 9The outer wall of the side rooms was about 8 3/4 feet thick. There was an open space between the side rooms of the temple 10and the rooms; it was about 35 feet wide all around the temple. 11The side rooms had doors opening onto the open space, one door on the north side and one on the south. The open space was about 8 3/4 feet wide all around. 12The building facing the separate area on the west side was about 122 1/2 feet wide. Its wall was about 8 3/4 feet thick all around, and it was about 157 1/2 feet long. 13Then he measured the temple: it was about 175 feet long. The separate area with the building and its walls was also about 175 feet long. 14The width of the temple’s front, together with the separate area, on the east side was about 175 feet. 15He measured the length of the building facing the separate area at the back of the temple, with its galleries on each side: it was about 175 feet. The main hall, the inner room and the porch facing the court 16the thresholds, the recessed windows, and the galleries around all three of them were paneled with wood all around, from the floor up to the windows. The windows were covered, 17even the space above the entrance into the inner room and outside it. On all the walls all around, both inside and outside, there were measured panels, 18carved with cherubim and palm trees, with a palm tree between each pair of cherubim. Each cherub had two faces: 19a human face turned toward the palm tree on one side, and a lion’s face turned toward the palm tree on the other. They were carved all around the whole temple. 20From the floor to above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the main hall. 21The doorframes of the main hall were square, and the front of the most holy place looked the same. 22There was an altar of wood about 5 1/4 feet high and about 3 1/2 feet long. Its corners, its length and its sides were wooden. He said to me, “This is the table that stands before the LORD.” 23The main hall and the most holy place each had a double door. 24Each door had two leaves that swung on hinges, two leaves for each door. 25On the doors of the main hall were carved cherubim and palm trees like those on the walls, and there was a wooden canopy over the front of the porch outside. 26There were recessed windows and palm trees on both sides of the porch, and on the side rooms of the temple and the canopies.
fields.summary: The man measures the temple’s inner rooms and decorations.

fields.title: Ezekiel 42
fields.body_html:
The priests’ holy rooms

1Then he led me out into the outer court on the north side and brought me to the rooms opposite the separate area and opposite the building on the north. 2The building with the north entrance was about 175 feet long and about 87 1/2 feet wide. 3It stood between the space of about 35 feet that belonged to the inner court and the pavement of the outer court, with gallery facing gallery on three levels. 4In front of the rooms, on the inner side, was a passage about 17 1/2 feet wide, a way of about 21 inches. Their doors faced north. 5The upper rooms were narrower, because the galleries took more space from them than from the rooms on the lower and middle floors of the building. 6The rooms were on three floors and had no pillars, as the courts had. So the top floor was set back more than the lower and middle floors. 7There was an outer wall parallel to the rooms, on the side toward the outer court, in front of the rooms. It was about 87 1/2 feet long. 8The rooms on the side of the outer court were about 87 1/2 feet long, while those facing the temple were about 175 feet long. 9Below these rooms was an entrance on the east side, for those going into them from the outer court. 10Along the wall of the court, starting from the east, facing the separate area and the building, there were rooms too. 11There was a passage in front of them. They looked like the rooms on the north side: they were the same length and width, with the same exits, the same plan and the same doors. 12The rooms on the south side had a door like these, at the head of the passage that ran in front of the matching wall on the east, for those going in. 13He said to me, “The north rooms and the south rooms that face the separate area are the holy rooms where the priests who come near to the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will put the most holy offerings: the grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering, for the place is holy. 14Once the priests have gone in, they are not to go out from the holy area into the outer court without leaving there the garments in which they serve, for these are holy. They must change into other clothes before they go near the area for the people.” 15When he had finished measuring the inner area of the temple, he led me out by the gate that faces east and measured the whole area around it. 16He measured the east side with the measuring reed: it was about a mile by the measuring reed. 17He measured the north side: it was about a mile by the measuring reed. 18He measured the south side: it was about a mile by the measuring reed. 19He turned to the west side and measured it: it was about a mile by the measuring reed. 20He measured it on all four sides. It had a wall all around it, about a mile long and about a mile wide, to separate what was holy from what was common.
fields.summary: The man measures the priests’ rooms and the outer wall.

fields.title: Ezekiel 43
fields.body_html:
The glory returns to the temple

1Then the man brought me to the gate, the one that faces east. 2And there was the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. The sound of its coming was like the roar of rushing waters, and the earth shone with his glory. 3What I saw in this vision was like what I had seen when I came to destroy the city, and like the vision I had seen by the Kebar Canal, and I fell face down. 4The glory of the LORD came into the temple through the gate that faces east. 5Then the Spirit lifted me and carried me into the inner court, and there the glory of the LORD was filling the temple. 6While the man stood beside me, I heard someone speak to me out of the temple. 7He said to me, “Son of man, here is my throne, and here is the place where my feet rest. Here I will live among the Israelites forever. Never again will the house of Israel defile my holy name, neither they nor their kings, with their prostitution and with the dead bodies of their kings at their high places, 8when they set their threshold by my threshold and their doorposts next to my doorposts, so that only a wall stood between me and them. By the detestable practices they committed they defiled my holy name, and so I destroyed them in my anger. 9Now let them put their prostitution and the dead bodies of their kings far away from me, and I will live among them forever.

The design of the temple and the altar

10As for you, son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, so that they will be ashamed of their sins, and let them study its plan. 11If they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the design of the temple, its arrangement, its exits and entrances, its whole design, and all its statutes and laws. Write it down where they can see it, so that they may keep its whole design and all its statutes and carry them out. 12This is the law of the temple: all the area around it on the top of the mountain will be most holy. This, then, is the law of the temple. 13These are the measurements of the altar in long cubits, each a cubit and a handbreadth: its gutter was about 21 inches deep and about 21 inches wide, with a rim of about 10 1/2 inches around its edge. This is the base of the altar. 14From the gutter on the ground up to the lower ledge was about 3 1/2 feet, and that ledge was about 21 inches wide. From the smaller ledge up to the larger ledge was about 7 feet, and that ledge was about 21 inches wide. 15The altar hearth was about 7 feet high, and from the altar hearth four horns projected upward. 16The altar hearth was square, about 21 feet long and about 21 feet wide. 17The upper ledge was also square, about 24 1/2 feet long and about 24 1/2 feet wide, with a rim of about 10 1/2 inches around it, and its gutter was about 21 inches all around. The altar’s steps faced east.” 18He said to me, “Son of man, the Lord GOD says this: These are the altar’s statutes for the day it is built, so that burnt offerings may be offered on it and blood splashed against it. 19You are to give a young bull for a sin offering to the Levitical priests of the family of Zadok, who come near to me to serve me, declares the Lord GOD. 20Take some of the blood and smear it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of the upper ledge and on the rim all around. In this way you will purify the altar and make atonement for it. 21Then take the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the designated part of the temple area, outside the sanctuary. 22On the second day you are to offer a male goat without defect as a sin offering, and the priests are to purify the altar as they did with the bull. 23When you have finished purifying it, you are to offer a young bull and a ram from the flock, both without defect. 24Bring them before the LORD, and the priests are to scatter salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD. 25For seven days you are to provide a goat each day as a sin offering, and a young bull and a ram from the flock, all without defect, are to be offered too. 26For seven days they are to make atonement for the altar and purify it. In this way they will dedicate it. 27When these days are over, from the eighth day on the priests are to present on the altar your burnt offerings and peace offerings, and I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD.”
fields.summary: The glory of God returns to the temple from the east and fills it, and the altar is dedicated.

fields.title: Ezekiel 44
fields.body_html:
The shut east gate

1Then the man brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east, and it was shut. 2The LORD said to me, “This gate is to stay shut. It must not be opened, and no one may come in through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has come in through it. Therefore it is to stay shut. 3Only the prince, because he is the prince, may sit in the gateway to eat a meal in the presence of the LORD. He is to come in by way of the porch of the gate and go out the same way.” 4Then the man brought me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked, and the glory of the LORD filled the LORD’s house, and I fell face down. 5The LORD said to me, “Son of man, pay close attention. Look carefully and listen closely to everything I tell you about all the statutes and laws of the LORD’s house. Note carefully who may enter the temple and who must be kept out of the sanctuary. 6Say to the rebellious house of Israel, the Lord GOD says this: Enough of all your detestable practices, house of Israel! 7You brought foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, into my sanctuary, defiling my temple while you offered me my food, the fat and the blood. You broke my covenant with all your detestable practices. 8You have not carried out your duty with my holy things yourselves, but you have put others in charge of my sanctuary for you. 9the Lord GOD says this: No foreigner who is uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter my sanctuary, not even one of the foreigners who live among the Israelites. 10But the Levites who moved far from me when Israel went astray and who strayed from me after their idols, must bear the consequences of their sin. 11They may serve in my sanctuary as guards at the gates of the temple and as its servants. They may slaughter the burnt offerings and the sacrifices for the people and stand before the people to serve them. 12Because they served the people in front of their idols and made the house of Israel stumble into sin, I have raised my hand in an oath against them, declares the Lord GOD, and they must bear the consequences of their sin. 13They are not to approach me to serve me as priests, nor to approach any of my holy things or the most holy offerings. They must bear their disgrace for the detestable practices they committed. 14Yet I will put them in charge of the duties of the temple, all its work and everything that has to be done in it.

The priests descended from Zadok

15But the Levitical priests, the descendants of Zadok, who carried out the duties of my sanctuary when the Israelites strayed from me, are to come near me to serve me. They are to stand before me to offer me the fat and the blood, declares the Lord GOD. 16They alone are to enter my sanctuary and come near my table to serve me and carry out my service. 17When they enter the gates of the inner court, they must wear linen clothes. They must have nothing made of wool on them while they serve at the gates of the inner court or inside the temple. 18Linen turbans are to be on their heads and linen undergarments on their hips; they must not put on anything that makes them sweat. 19When they go out to the people in the outer court, they must take off the clothes they wore while they served and leave them in the holy rooms. They must put on other clothes, so that they do not pass on holiness to the people through their clothes. 20They must neither shave their heads nor let their hair grow long; they must keep their hair trimmed. 21No priest may drink wine when he is to enter the inner court. 22They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only virgins of Israelite descent, or a widow whose husband was a priest. 23They are to teach my people the difference between what is holy and what is common, and show them how to tell the unclean from the clean. 24In a dispute they are to act as judges and decide it according to my rulings. They are to keep my laws and my statutes at all my appointed festivals, and they are to keep my Sabbaths holy. 25A priest must not make himself unclean by going near a dead body. But he may make himself unclean for his father or mother, son or daughter, brother, or a sister who had no husband. 26After he has been cleansed, he must wait seven more days. 27When he enters the sanctuary again, into the inner court, to serve in the sanctuary, he must offer a sin offering for himself, declares the Lord GOD. 28Their inheritance is to be this: I am their inheritance. You are not to give them property in Israel; I am their property. 29They are to eat the grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering, and everything in Israel devoted to the LORD is to be theirs. 30The best of all the firstfruits of every kind and every special gift of every kind from all your gifts will belong to the priests. You are also to give the priest the first portion of your dough, so that a blessing may rest on your household. 31The priests must not eat anything, whether bird or animal, that has died of itself or been killed by wild animals.
fields.summary: The east gate is closed for God has entered through it. Only the Levites of Zadok’s line may serve as priests.

fields.title: Ezekiel 45
fields.body_html:
The holy portion of the land

1When you allot the land as an inheritance, you are to set apart a special portion for the LORD, a holy portion of the land, about 8 1/4 miles long and about 3 1/3 miles wide. All of it will be holy. 2Of this area, a square about 880 feet on each side is to be for the sanctuary, with about 87 1/2 feet of open land around it. 3In the area you measure, you are to mark off a section about 8 1/4 miles long and about 3 1/3 miles wide. The sanctuary, the most holy place, will be in it. 4This holy portion of the land is to belong to the priests who serve in the sanctuary, who come near to serve the LORD. It will be a place for their houses and a holy area for the sanctuary. 5Another area about 8 1/4 miles long and about 3 1/3 miles wide is to belong to the Levites who serve in the temple, as their property: twenty rooms. 6As the city’s property you are to assign an area about 1 2/3 miles wide and about 8 1/4 miles long, next to the holy portion. It will belong to the whole house of Israel. 7The prince is to have the land on both sides of the holy portion and the city’s property, next to the holy portion and the city’s property, reaching west from the western side and east from the eastern side, its length matching one of the tribal portions, from the western border to the eastern border. 8This land is to be his property in Israel. Then my princes will no longer oppress my people, but will let the house of Israel have the land according to their tribes.

Honest rulers and honest measures

9the Lord GOD says this: Enough, princes of Israel! Put an end to violence and destruction, and do what is just and right. Stop driving my people off their land, declares the Lord GOD. 10You are to use honest scales, an honest ephah and an honest bath. 11The ephah and the bath are to be the same size, the bath holding about 6 gallons and the ephah about 6 gallons. The homer is to be the standard for both. 12The shekel is to be twenty gerahs. Your mina is to be about 8 ounces plus about 10 ounces plus about 6 ounces. 13This is the special offering you are to give: about a gallon from every 6 bushels of wheat, and about a gallon from every 6 bushels of barley. 14The portion of oil, measured by the bath, is to be about 2 1/2 quarts from every 60 gallons (a kor is ten baths, the same as a homer, for ten baths make a homer). 15and one sheep out of every 200 from the well-watered pastures of Israel. These will be used for grain offerings, burnt offerings and peace offerings, to make atonement on the people’s behalf, declares the Lord GOD. 16All the people of the land are to give this special offering to the prince in Israel. 17The prince is to be responsible for the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the drink offerings at the festivals, the new moons and the Sabbaths, at all the appointed festivals of the house of Israel. He is to supply the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings and peace offerings that make atonement for the house of Israel.

The yearly festivals

18the Lord GOD says this: In the first month, on its first day, you are to take a young bull without defect and purify the sanctuary. 19The priest is to take some blood from the sin offering and smear it on the temple doorposts, on the four corners of the altar’s upper ledge and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court. 20You are to do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins by mistake or without knowing it. In this way you will make atonement for the temple. 21On the fourteenth day of the first month you are to celebrate the Passover, a festival lasting seven days, during which bread made without yeast is to be eaten. 22On that day the prince is to provide a young bull as a sin offering on behalf of himself and all the people of the land. 23During the seven days of the festival he is to provide seven young bulls and seven rams without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD each day for the seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering. 24He is to provide a grain offering of about 6 gallons for each bull and about 6 gallons for each ram, together with about a gallon of oil for each ephah. 25In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day, at the festival, he is to make the same provision for seven days: the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings and oil.
fields.summary: A portion of land is set apart for God, the priests, the city and the prince, and offerings and festivals are ordered.

fields.title: Ezekiel 46
fields.body_html:
Offerings for Sabbaths and new moons

1the Lord GOD says this: The gate of the inner court that faces east is to stay shut during the six working days, but it is to be opened on the Sabbath and at the new moon. 2The prince is to come in from outside through the porch of the gate and stand by the doorpost of the gate. The priests are to offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he is to bow down in worship at the threshold of the gate and then go out. But the gate is not to be shut until evening. 3The people of the land are to bow down in worship before the LORD at the entrance of that gate on the Sabbaths and the new moons. 4The burnt offering that the prince offers to the LORD on the Sabbath day is to be six lambs without defect and a ram without defect, 5with a grain offering of about 6 gallons for the ram, and for the lambs as much as he chooses to give, with about a gallon of oil for each ephah. 6On the day of the new moon he is to offer a young bull without defect, and six lambs and a ram, all without defect. 7He is to provide a grain offering of about 6 gallons with the bull and about 6 gallons with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he can, together with about a gallon of oil for each ephah. 8When the prince enters, he is to come in through the porch of the gate and go out the same way. 9At the appointed festivals, when the people of the land come before the LORD, those who come in by the north gate to worship are to go out by the south gate, and those who come in by the south gate are to go out by the north gate. No one is to go back through the gate by which they came in; each is to go straight out the opposite side. 10The prince is to be among them, coming in when they come in and going out when they go out. 11At the festivals and the appointed feasts the grain offering is to be about 6 gallons with a bull and about 6 gallons with a ram, and with the lambs as much as he chooses to give, together with about a gallon of oil for each ephah.

Freewill offerings and the daily offering

12When the prince provides a freewill offering to the LORD, whether a burnt offering or peace offerings, the gate facing east is to be opened for him, and he is to present his burnt offering or his peace offerings just as on the Sabbath day. When he goes out, the gate is to be shut behind him. 13Every day you are to provide a lamb a year old without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD; you are to provide it morning after morning. 14With it you are to provide a grain offering every morning: about a gallon of flour and about 1 1/4 quarts of oil to moisten the fine flour. This grain offering to the LORD is a lasting statute, to be kept continually. 15So the lamb, the grain offering and the oil are to be provided every morning as a regular burnt offering.

The prince’s land

16the Lord GOD says this: If the prince makes a gift of land to any of his sons, it will become part of the son’s inheritance. It will belong to his sons as their property by inheritance. 17But if he makes one of his servants a gift from his inheritance, the servant may keep it until the year of release. Then it will go back to the prince. His inheritance belongs to his sons alone. 18The prince must not take any of the people’s inheritance, driving them off their property. He is to give his sons their inheritance out of what he himself owns, so that none of my people will be scattered from their property.” 19Then the man led me through the entrance beside the gate to the priests’ holy rooms facing north, and there I saw a place at the far western end.

The temple kitchens

20He said to me, “This is the place where the priests are to boil the guilt offering and the sin offering and bake the grain offering, so that they do not bring them out into the outer court and pass on holiness to the people.” 21Then he brought me out into the outer court and took me around to each of its four corners. In each corner of the court there was another small court. 22In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, about 70 feet long and about 52 1/2 feet wide. All four corner courts were the same size. 23Around the inside of each of the four courts ran a ledge of stone, with places for cooking built under the ledges all around. 24He said to me, “These are the kitchens where those who serve in the temple are to boil the people’s sacrifices.”
fields.summary: The prince and the people worship at the appointed times, and rules are given for the prince’s property.

fields.title: Ezekiel 47
fields.body_html:
The river flowing from the temple

1The man led me back to the temple’s entrance. Water was coming out from beneath the threshold of the temple and flowing east, since the temple faced east. It ran down from beneath the south side of the temple, south of the altar. 2Then he took me out by the north gate and brought me around outside to the outer east gate. There the water was trickling out on the south side. 3As the man went out toward the east with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off about 1,750 feet and led me through the water. It came up to my ankles. 4He measured off another about 1,750 feet and led me through the water, and it came up to my knees. He measured off another about 1,750 feet and led me through, and the water came up to my waist. 5Again he measured off about 1,750 feet, and now it was a river too deep for me to cross, for the water had risen. It was deep enough to swim in, a river no one could cross. 6He said to me, “Son of man, do you see this?” Then he led me back to the bank of the river. 7As I came back, I saw a great many trees on both banks of the river. 8He said to me, “This water goes out toward the eastern region and down into the Arabah, and it goes into the sea. When it flows into the Dead Sea, its salt water will be made fresh. 9Wherever the river flows, every kind of living creature that swarms will live. There will be a great many fish, because this water flows there and makes the salt water fresh. Wherever the river goes, everything will live. 10Fishermen will stand along its shore from En-gedi to En-eglaim, and it will be a place for spreading out nets. Its fish will be of as many kinds as the fish of the Great Sea, and very many. 11But its swamps and marshes will not be made fresh; they will be kept for salt. 12On both banks of the river every kind of tree that bears food will grow. Their leaves will never wither, and their fruit will never fail. They will bear fresh fruit every month, because their water flows from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food and their leaves for healing.”

The borders of the land

13the Lord GOD says this: This is the boundary by which you will divide the land among the twelve tribes of Israel as their inheritance, with two portions for Joseph. 14You are to divide it equally among you, since I raised my hand in an oath to give it to your ancestors. This land will fall to you as your inheritance. 15This is to be the border of the land: On the north side it will run from the Great Sea by the Hethlon road to Lebo, to Zedad, 16Hamath, Berothah and Sibraim, which lie between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath, as far as Hazer-hattikon, on the border of Hauran. 17So the border is to run from the sea to Hazar-enan, on the Damascus border, with Hamath’s territory lying to the north. This is the northern side. 18On the east side, the border is to pass between Hauran and Damascus, and along the Jordan between Gilead and the land of Israel. You are to measure it from the northern border to the eastern sea. This is the eastern side. 19On the south side, the border will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, along the Wadi of Egypt to the Great Sea. This is the southern side. 20On the west side, the Great Sea will be the border, up to a point opposite Lebo-hamath. This is the western side. 21You are to divide this land among yourselves by the tribes of Israel. 22You are to allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the outsiders living among you who have had children among you. You are to treat them as native-born Israelites; they are to receive an inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel. 23In whatever tribe an outsider lives, there you are to give him his inheritance, declares the Lord GOD.
fields.summary: A river flows from the temple, growing deeper and bringing life wherever it goes. The borders of the land are set.

fields.title: Ezekiel 48
fields.body_html:
The portions of the tribes

1These are the names of the tribes and their portions. At the northern end, along the Hethlon road to Lebo-hamath, as far as Hazar-enan on the Damascus border, with Hamath lying to the north, reaching from the east side to the west, Dan is to have one portion. 2Asher is to have one portion, bordering Dan from the east side to the west side. 3Naphtali is to have one portion, bordering Asher from the east side to the west side. 4Manasseh is to have one portion, bordering Naphtali from the east side to the west side. 5Ephraim is to have one portion, bordering Manasseh from the east side to the west side. 6Reuben is to have one portion, bordering Ephraim from the east side to the west side. 7Judah is to have one portion, bordering Reuben from the east side to the west side. 8Next to Judah’s territory, from the east side to the west side, will be the special portion you are to set apart. It is to be about 8 1/4 miles wide, and as long as one of the tribal portions from the east side to the west, with the sanctuary in the middle of it. 9The special portion that you are to set apart for the LORD is to be about 8 1/4 miles long and about 3 1/3 miles wide. 10This holy portion is to belong to the priests. It is to measure about 8 1/4 miles on the north side, about 3 1/3 miles on the west side, about 3 1/3 miles on the east side and about 8 1/4 miles on the south side. The sanctuary of the LORD is to be in the middle of it. 11It is for the consecrated priests, the descendants of Zadok, who carried out my service. They did not stray when the Israelites strayed, as the Levites did.

The Levites, the city and the prince

12It will be a special gift to them from the special portion of the land, a most holy area next to the territory of the Levites. 13Alongside the priests’ territory the Levites are to have an area about 8 1/4 miles long and about 3 1/3 miles wide. The whole length is to be about 8 1/4 miles and the width about 3 1/3 miles. 14They must not sell any of it or exchange it, and this best part of the land must not pass to anyone else, for it is holy to the LORD. 15The remaining area, about 1 2/3 miles wide and about 8 1/4 miles long, is to be for the ordinary use of the city, for houses and for open land. The city is to be in the middle of it. 16These are to be its measurements: the north side about 1 1/2 miles, the south side about 1 1/2 miles, the east side about 1 1/2 miles and the west side about 1 1/2 miles. 17The city’s open land is to be about 440 feet wide on the north, about 440 feet on the south, about 440 feet on the east and about 440 feet on the west. 18The rest of the length alongside the holy portion, about 3 1/3 miles on the east and about 3 1/3 miles on the west, will run alongside the holy portion. Its crops are to be food for the workers of the city. 19The workers of the city, who will come from all the tribes of Israel, are to farm it. 20The whole special portion is to be a square, about 8 1/4 miles on each side. You are to set apart the holy portion together with the city’s property. 21What is left on both sides of the holy portion and the city’s property is to belong to the prince. It will reach east from the about 8 1/4 miles of the special portion to the eastern border, and west from the about 8 1/4 miles to the western border, alongside the tribal portions. This will belong to the prince. The holy portion, with the sanctuary of the temple, will be in the middle of it. 22The property of the Levites and the property of the city will lie in the middle of the prince’s land. The land between the territory of Judah and the territory of Benjamin is to belong to the prince. 23As for the rest of the tribes: Benjamin is to have one portion, from the east side to the west side. 24Simeon is to have one portion, bordering Benjamin from the east side to the west side. 25Issachar is to have one portion, bordering Simeon from the east side to the west side. 26Zebulun is to have one portion, bordering Issachar from the east side to the west side. 27Gad is to have one portion, bordering Zebulun from the east side to the west side. 28On the south side of Gad’s territory, the border is to run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, along the Wadi of Egypt to the Great Sea. 29This is the land you are to divide by lot as an inheritance among the tribes of Israel, and these are their portions, declares the Lord GOD.

The gates of the city

30These are to be the exits of the city: On the north side, which is about 1 1/2 miles long, 31there will be three gates: one for Reuben, one for Judah and one for Levi. The gates of the city are to be named after the tribes of Israel. 32On the east side, which is about 1 1/2 miles long, there will be three gates: one for Joseph, one for Benjamin and one for Dan. 33On the south side, which measures about 1 1/2 miles, there will be three gates: one for Simeon, one for Issachar and one for Zebulun. 34On the west side, which is about 1 1/2 miles long, there will be three gates: one for Gad, one for Asher and one for Naphtali. 35The distance around the city will be about 6 miles. And from that day the name of the city will be The LORD Is There.
fields.summary: The land is divided among the tribes, and the city will be named for God’s presence there.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
The distance around the city will be about 6 miles. And from that day the name of the city will be The LORD Is There.

— Ezekiel 48:35

Ezekiel ends with a name. After nine chapters of measurements, gates and tribal boundaries, the last words of the book give the city its title, and it is not Jerusalem. It is “The LORD Is There.” The book that began with the glory of God appearing to exiles far from home, and went on to watch that glory leave the temple, closes with a city whose whole identity is that God lives in it and will not leave again.

The question the book leaves with you

Ezekiel’s first hearers asked whether God had abandoned them. The book answers in two ways that belong together. First, he had left the temple, because they had filled it with idols and driven him out; his holiness is not to be taken for granted or tamed. Second, he had never left them. He was a sanctuary to them in Babylon. His throne had wheels. He would gather them, cleanse them, give them a new heart and his own Spirit, and dwell among them for ever.

So the question Ezekiel leaves is the one God asked him in the valley: “can these bones live?” It is asked of every life that has gone dry, every church that has lost its fire, every people who say “our hope is gone; we are completely cut off.” Ezekiel’s answer was not optimism. It was “Lord GOD, only you know,” and then obedience: he prophesied as he was told, and the breath came. The book’s other question is pressed with equal force: “Why would you die, house of Israel?” God takes no pleasure in the death of anyone. “So turn back and live!”

Where the book points

Much of what Ezekiel promised began to come true when the exiles returned. But the New Testament sees its fullness in Christ. Jesus called himself the good shepherd who searches for the lost and lays down his life for the sheep, the shepherd of David’s line that Ezekiel foretold. He spoke of the Spirit as rivers of living water, and of being born of water and the Spirit. On the day of Pentecost God put his Spirit within his people, and Paul could call the church God’s temple.

The last book of the Bible is full of Ezekiel. John sees the four living creatures around the throne, eats a scroll that is sweet in his mouth, hears of Gog and Magog, watches an angel measure the holy city, and is shown at last a river of the water of life flowing from the throne, with the tree of life on its banks, whose “leaves bring healing to the nations.” Ezekiel’s city called “The LORD Is There” becomes the new Jerusalem, where “God’s dwelling is with human beings.”

Where to go from here

Ezekiel has given preachers some of their most searching texts, and many of the best sermons on them are in this library. A few places to begin:

  • On turning and living (Ezekiel 18 and 33). Richard Baxter’s A Call to the Unconverted, a whole book on 33:11, one of the most widely read evangelistic books of the seventeenth century; and Charles G. Finney’s sermon Sinners Bound to Change Their Own Hearts (18:31).
  • On the new heart and the Spirit within (Ezekiel 36). Charles H. Spurgeon’s sermons The New Heart (36:26), Free Grace (36:32) and Prayer—the Forerunner of Mercy (36:37), and “The Necessity of the Spirit’s Work” (36:27) in Spurgeon on the Holy Spirit; Andrew Murray’s chapter “New Covenant Obedience” in The Two Covenants, also on 36:27.
  • On the valley of dry bones (Ezekiel 37). Cyril of Jerusalem’s The Catechetical Lectures, whose Lecture XVIII opens with Ezekiel 37 and teaches the resurrection of the body from it.
  • On the prophet and his visions. A. B. Simpson’s chapter “The Holy Spirit in Ezekiel”, in The Holy Spirit, or Power from on High, Part I; and Augustine’s The City of God, Book XVIII, chapter 34, on what Ezekiel and Daniel foretold of Christ.

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to Ezekiel in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, chapter by chapter, what the great writers of the church have said about each passage of this book.

Then read Ezekiel beside Jeremiah, his older contemporary, who was saying the same things in Jerusalem while Ezekiel said them in Babylon, and beside the Revelation to John, which takes up his visions at the end of the Bible. And when hope seems dry, come back to the valley, where a mortal stood among the bones and was asked a question only God could answer:

He asked me, “Son of man, can these bones live?” I answered, “Lord GOD, only you know.”

— Ezekiel 37:3
